detail.abstract: The effectiveness of conventional technical indicators in deep learning-based financial forecasting remains an open empirical question. This study presents a large-scale ablation analysis of their contribution to next-day price prediction using recurrent neural networks. We conduct 500 controlled experiments across 10 assets representing five asset classes: commodities, cryptocurrencies, equities, foreign exchange, and market indices, using daily OHLCV data from 2010 to 2025. Five feature configurations are evaluated: raw OHLCV inputs and four indicator-augmented variants incorporating momentum, trend, volatility, and all indicators. Each configuration is assessed using LSTM and GRU architectures across five random seeds. Results demonstrate that technical indicators generally fail to improve forecasting performance and frequently increase prediction errors. The raw OHLCV baseline achieves the lowest mean RMSE (0.166 ± 0.148) and highest mean directional accuracy (55.7% ± 5.5%). The comprehensive indicator configuration increases RMSE by 34.6% (𝑝 < 0.001, Cohen's 𝑑 =-0.29), while all four indicator categories exhibit statistically significant performance degradation at 𝛼 = 0.05. GRU models achieve higher directional accuracy than LSTM models (55.3% versus 51.0%), although their RMSE difference is not statistically significant (𝑝 = 0.846). Foreign exchange is the only asset class benefiting from volatility indicators, with a 4.2% RMSE reduction, whereas cryptocurrencies and commodities exhibit 83% higher mean prediction error than lower-volatility assets. These findings suggest that recurrent networks may implicitly learn patterns represented by conventional indicators, rendering explicit indicator features redundant or detrimental. The results underscore the importance of rigorous baseline comparisons and evidence-driven feature selection in neural network-based financial forecasting.

detail.abstract: Most of the economics and legal literature on "The Coase Theorem" (TCT) tends to focus on two related aspects of the TCT: the idea of transaction costs and the idea of efficient bargaining. The focus of this Article, by contrast, is on the underlying logical premise of TCT: specifically, the idea of "reciprocal" harms. The remainder of this Article is organized as follows. Building on my previous work, Part I begins by revisiting the most memorable and picturesque of Ronald Coase's illustrations of reciprocal harms: the rancher-farmer fable in his landmark social cost paper. Part II then pinpoints the very first time Coase uses the word "reciprocal" to describe the problem of harmful effects, Coase's pioneering paper on The Federal Communications Commission. Next, Part III traces the intellectual origins of Coase's reciprocal-harm model. In summary, potential precursors that paved the way into Coase's idea of reciprocal harms include Wesley Hohfeld's theory of legal relations; what economist Jim Buchanan has called the "LSE tradition in cost theory"; Frank Knight's critique of A. C. Pigou; and Sir Arnold Plant, the British economist who by Coase's own admission had the largest influence on Coase's intellectual development. Part IV then concludes by exploring the domain or scope of Coase's reciprocal-harm model: to which harms does this model apply: economic harms, involuntary harms more generally (e.g. negligence), or all harms? This Article thus makes three new contributions to the literature on the Coase theorem: it describes Ronald Coase's insight that harms are a reciprocal problem as an axiom or truism; it traces the intellectual origins of this counter-intuitive idea; and it explores the domain or outer limits of Coase's reciprocal-harm axiom.

detail.abstract: We study how preference structure affects the existence and uniqueness of fair and strategyproof budget aggregation rules. Under Leontief preferences and any fixed vector of strictly positive budget shares, group-strategyproofness and weighted core fair share characterize the weighted Nash product rule, with no continuity assumption. With equal shares, this removes the continuity requirement from the characterization of Brandt et al. (Mathematics of Operations Research, 2025). With fixed unequal donations, it removes the U-continuity requirement from Greger's (2024) characterization. In contrast, under distance preferences induced by a common strictly convex, coordinate-permutation-invariant norm, no deterministic rule satisfies strategyproofness and core fair share when there are at least two agents and three projects. This follows from a stronger impossibility that requires only Pareto efficiency and single-minded positive share in addition to strategyproofness. It applies to every ℓ r norm with 1 < r < ∞, and together with known endpoint results it shows that strategyproofness, Pareto efficiency, and proportionality are incompatible for every 1 ≤ r ≤ ∞ when there are at least three agents and three projects. These results answer the continuity and all-ℓ r proportionality questions raised by Brandt et al.

detail.abstract:
This study utilizes publicly traded U.S. military-industrial enterprises as analytical samples to examine the mechanisms through which the capital market paradigm of shareholder value maximization restructures the organizational logic of the defense industrial base, thereby undermining the wartime mobilization capacity and strategic autonomy of modern nation-states.

The findings indicate that when defense enterprises undergo a cultural shift from an engineering-centric model to a financially oriented paradigm, their optimization priorities cease to emphasize inventory redundancy, supply chain autarky, and long-term technological accumulation, and instead prioritize share repurchases, dividend distributions, outsourcing, and high-unit-price platform-based delivery.

This financialized military-industrial system demonstrates elevated returns on equity and valuation metrics during peacetime; however, it manifests a critical "magazine depth" deficit during actual conflicts—characterized by severely depleted inventories of interceptors and conventional munitions, a contracting foundational manufacturing ecosystem, and extended delivery timelines spanning multiple years.

Drawing upon empirical analysis of the Boeing case, inventory data for THAAD and Patriot systems, the 2026 Trump executive order, and the structural configuration of the military-industrial iron triangle, this paper contends that an excessively developed equity market, when decoupled from industrial capital constraints, constitutes a systemic threat to national security.

detail.abstract: How can technical change be directed toward socially valuable but privately under-supplied technologies such as green innovation? The most studied levers, such as carbon pricing and environmental regulation, operate on firms from the outside. We study an overlooked lever within the firm, CEO inside debt, and find it positively associated with both the quantity and quality of green patents. This result is striking because debt-like compensation is known to heighten managerial risk aversion and induce conservative investment and financing policies, including reduced R&D. The relationship strengthens among firms with greater environmental risk exposure (the risk-management channel), firms led by longer-tenured or younger CEOs (the horizonalignment channel), and firms with stronger stakeholder and sustainability orientations (the sustainability-alignment channel). Our findings highlight a conventional firm-level incentive design that is not linked to ESG metrics but can complement public policies in mitigating the double-externality problem associated with green innovation.

detail.abstract: We estimate the causal effect of a first-half yellow card on the booked player's defensive behaviour in the second half of the same match, where a second booking means dismissal. Using open event data on 2,440 matches from the five major European leagues, we apply double machine learning to adjust for a high-dimensional set of pre-treatment confounders and bound selective substitution with trimming bounds. Opponent-directed defensive actions decline by an estimated 6.4%, with fouls falling by 27.2% and pressures by 5.1%, while tackles and ball-directed actions show no change. The reduction appears immediately after the restart, persists to full time, and is concentrated among defensive midfielders and players whose team is not trailing. Teammates of booked players increase their fouling by 4.5%, and booked players are withdrawn at half-time twice as often as comparable unbooked players. The results provide causal, player-level evidence of within-match deterrence in football.

detail.abstract: This technical note introduces tabular foundation models (TFMs) to accounting research and evaluates their performance in one common benchmark task: predicting firms’ next-year earnings changes. TFMs produce numeric predictions and learn in context, without post-release training or tuning, making them natural and easy to use for forecasting. The TFMs we study are pretrained on synthetic tabular data, so they avoid look-ahead bias from memorizing firms’ outcomes. We compare Google Research’s TabFM with a fine-tuned open-weight large language model developed in recent accounting research and with several tree-based models. TabFM is more accurate than all comparison models. It is also faster and less computationally intensive than the large language model. Several tree-based specifications produce predictions more quickly than TabFM, so choosing between them involves a trade-off between accuracy and speed. We conclude that TFMs have promise as a new tool for forecasting in accounting and finance. However, our evaluation is based on a single benchmark task, and no class of models is likely to dominate in all settings.

detail.abstract: Virtual bidding in ERCOT is a daily allocation problem: a book with per-hour MW caps and per-day MWh budgets must decide which hours at which hubs receive volume. Given spread forecasts, the allocation is a continuous knapsack whose greedy ll is exact. We ask whether reinforcement learning can improve the forecast ranking of hours. Using a regimeaware front-end to generate state features, we ne-tune a PPO agent that supplies priorities to the knapsack and compare it with the forecast-driven allocation it starts from over 380 out-of-sample days at ve ERCOT hubs. The verdict rule was xed before the deciding experiment; results are medians over three independent training runs. Two conditions are necessary. Without a behaviour-cloned prior and day-episodic credit assignment, PPO follows a proxy of the forecast and destroys the allocation. With both, the agent retains 86% of the allocation's gross and passes the per-hub test at two of ve hubs, one only because netuning left an abstaining prior untouched, but does not beat the allocation, and the verdict is a fail. Beyond the verdict, the sum of per-hub worst days is 1.4 times the allocation's, longer ne-tuning drifts farther from the prior, and the spread across training runs is wide where the agent departs late. An ablation ladder isolates each condition, an action probe reveals what the policy reads, and a public-input forecast serves as control. The contribution is a negative result and the conditions required to avoid degrading a forecast-driven knapsack.

detail.abstract: Credit card holders have long been classified as either revolvers, who carry balances, or transactors, who pay in full. This binary label ignores partial payers, the direction in which payment behavior is moving, and the reliability of the history it rests on. We propose a five-state framework, developed from practitioner experience, that classifies applicants at the application stage by payment level and direction of change: Persistent Transactor, Persistent Revolver, Partial, Emerging Revolver and Improving Revolver, while applicants without recent card history are reported but not classified. States are assigned by an ordered, exhaustive decision tree, with a change threshold scaled to the amount of observed history and all thresholds estimated without outcome data. On the public Home Credit Default Risk dataset, 38,131 of the 86,905 applicants holding at least one credit card (43.9%) have enough recent history to be classified. The states raise the holdout AUC for default from 0.708 with external credit scores alone to 0.718 (+0.010, 95% CI +0.005 to +0.016); Persistent Revolvers have 2.2 times the default odds of Persistent Transactors at the same scores. Almost all of this gain comes from the level dimension. The direction dimension instead predicts future payment behavior: measured twelve months earlier, Emerging Revolvers have 1.5 times and Improving Revolvers 0.38 times the odds of revolving a year later, beyond their twelve-month payment levels. The rule-based states match or exceed k-means and Gaussian-mixture segmentations for default prediction while remaining interpretable, and are robust to most design choices. A simulation shows that fixed change thresholds falsely flag 28–51% of stable wallets with two to five cards, that thresholds must be calibrated to the discrete set of attainable shift values, and that comparing two separate six-month periods roughly doubles detection power relative to nested windows. We discuss uses in prescreening, test design, marketing and credit policy.

detail.abstract: Reversible solid oxide cells are expected to follow variable electricity, reverse mode and run on hydrogen, steam or methane-containing fuels, which calls for stack models that resolve the internal state, treat both modes and the fuel chemistry together and remain cheap enough for system simulation. This paper presents a one-dimensional dynamic model of a reversible solid oxide cell in OpenModelica, with a unified reversible closure and a reactive-node formulation of the gas channels in which reforming and shift sources act where they are evaluated. It is validated locally against a four-cell SolydEra short stack whose top cell carries twenty current-measuring segments and thermocouples. With one parameter set identified on first-campaign polarisation data, it reproduces the polarisation curves in both modes and five electrolysis ramps at 650–750 °C with mean errors of 17 mV on cell voltage, 0.86 K on column temperatures and 0.022 A cm⁻² on column current densities; it captures the thermal transient of an electrolysis-to-fuel-cell reversal (t63 735 vs 705 s) without adjusting thermal parameters, the open-circuit cooling caused by stepwise methane addition (−26.5 vs −24.7 K per NL min⁻¹) with literature kinetics, and the current distribution on methane–steam at steam-to-carbon 2.2 within 0.011 A cm⁻². The reactive-node scheme halves the voltage error of the explicit upwind construction on hydrogen–steam ramps and alone accepts hydrogen-free methane feeds. Changes of cell state over five months are reported rather than fitted away. The model runs at 0.01–0.12 of real time for a four-cell stack, qualifying it for system-level dynamic simulation.

title: Eliminating Polarity Hallucinations and Order Book Horizon Truncation Bias in Autonomous Multi-Agent Quantitative Systems: Schmitt-Trigger Factor Ontologies, Scroll-Out Resistant Deep OFI, and Slippage-Proof Pyramiding

detail.abstract:
Autonomous financial trading architectures driven by Large Language Models (LLMs) and high-frequency Limit Order Book (LOB) telemetry suffer from three structural failure modes that degrade out-of-sample Sharpe ratios and induce tail-risk drawdowns in live execution: (1) Semantic Polarity Inversion, wherein generative agents misinterpret inverse valuation or macro-stress indicators (e.g., EV/EBITDA, credit spreads) as positively correlated with forward returns, combined with Boundary Chattering when factor z-scores oscillate across decision thresholds; (2) Order Book Horizon Truncation Bias (The Scroll-Out Spoofing Illusion), a microstructure distortion in finite K-level moving-window order book feeds where rapid upward price appreciation causes resting bid liquidity to drop below the K-th visible depth horizon, falsely mimicking malicious institutional spoofing cancellations; and (3) Pyramiding Ruin Under Jump Slippage, where adding exposure to winning positions elevates the aggregate break-even price to a level vulnerable to gap-down stop-loss slippage.

In this paper, we formulate a unified mathematical framework to eliminate all three vulnerabilities. First, we introduce Deterministic Factor Ontology Contracts coupled with a Discrete-Time Schmitt-Trigger Hysteresis Operator featuring a symmetric deadband [-delta, +delta] that guarantees zero polarity inversion and suppresses signal chattering under local Brownian noise. Second, we prove that naive depth-disappearance estimators exhibit deterministic false-positive spoofing bias during momentum breakouts, and we construct a Scroll-Out Resistant Deep Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) Estimator utilizing a visible-window boundary invariant (P_bid,K <= p <= P_bid,1), trade-volume subtraction, and sub-second twin-snapshot differentials (dt = 0.12 s). Third, we derive the exact closed-form Slippage-Proof Pyramiding Boundary Inequality, establishing the maximum tolerable stop-loss slippage under which a pyramided position retains strictly positive worst-case realized profit. We validate the architecture across 1,000 property-based formal verification trajectories (Hypothesis/oss-fuzz) with zero invariant violations, Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (15 splits, PBO = 20.0%), Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR = 97.76%), and 10,000-run Monte Carlo stress testing (0.00% risk of ruin) across a 5-year empirical sample (2021-2026).

detail.abstract: We study when greater dispersion of bargainers' ideal points moves the symmetric Nash bargaining policy toward the status quo without changing the unanimously acceptable policy set. In a one-dimensional model with a common symmetric, strictly convex loss function, the closest ideal point fixes that set. For every fixed $n \ge 3$, we characterize universal dispersion contraction through right-side concavity of the individual Nash score and an $n$-dependent feasibility restriction. The latter is vacuous with three bargainers but can bind with four. Under a tail-growth condition, quadratic loss, up to positive scaling, is the only loss function guaranteeing contraction for any fixed $n \ge 4$. More strongly, for any nonquadratic loss satisfying that condition and strict right-side score concavity, adding a fourth bargainer can reverse the response to the same mean-preserving spread among the original three, despite an unchanged agreement set. Smooth power losses illustrate this result. We also exhibit a nonquadratic exception outside the tail-growth class and establish bounded-domain robustness under small nonquadratic perturbations of quadratic loss, uniformly over population sizes.

title: Suppressing Sycophancy Cascades and Trauma Lock-In in Autonomous Financial Multi-Agent LLMs: Bounded Adversarial Deliberation, Exponential Time-Decay Episodic Memory, and Foundation Model OOD Veto
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Suppressing Sycophancy Cascades and Trauma Lock-In in Autonomous Financial Multi-Agent LLMs: Bounded Adversarial Deliberation, Exponential Time-Decay Episodic Memory, and Foundation Model OOD Veto

detail.abstract:
Autonomous financial decision-making architectures powered by Large Language Model (LLM) ensembles and episodic verbal reinforcement learning (Reflexion / Retrieval-Augmented Generation) exhibit three structural cognitive pathologies when deployed across non-stationary market regimes: (1) Sycophancy Cascades (Herding Amplification), wherein sequential multi-agent debate induces conformist token generation that collapses cross-sectional stance variance and amplifies false-positive entries during speculative market tops; (2) Episodic Trauma Lock-In (Learned Helplessness in Lexical Memory), where retrieving historical stop-loss reflections via time-invariant BM25 similarity allows severe drawdown clusters from past bear markets to permanently dominate top-k context windows even after macroeconomic recovery, freezing capital in perpetual HOLD states; and (3) Time-Series Foundation Model Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Hallucination, where pre-trained zero-shot forecasters (Google TimesFM, Amazon Chronos) extrapolate bullish price trajectories on structurally insolvent equities experiencing institutional order-book distribution.

Building upon the deterministic microstructure and factor ontology invariants established in Hashimoto (2026a), we formulate a unified mathematical framework to eliminate all three cognitive failure modes. First, we construct a Parallel Blind Orthogonal Evaluation Protocol paired with a Bounded Adversarial Debate Perturbation Operator (|dS_i| <= kappa_max) and an HTTP 429 Degraded Defense-Only Circuit Breaker that guarantees zero blind execution during LLM inference blackouts. Second, we introduce a Time-Decayed Compound-Token BM25 Episodic Memory Kernel featuring an exponential half-life attenuation factor w(dt) = 2^(-dt / tau_half) (tau_half = 30.0 days) and derive the closed-form Trauma Horizon Escape Inequality governing optimal memory forgetting across regime transitions. Third, we establish a Deterministic Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Absolute Veto Operator that overrides foundation-model bullish hallucinations whenever fundamental solvency and 10-level Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) breach structural safety bounds. Empirical ablation across a 5-year multi-asset dataset (2021-2026) and 20 automated chaos-engineering unit tests confirms a 0.0% trauma lock-in rate, a 71.4% reduction in herd-driven false breakouts, and 100% immunity to foundation-model OOD hallucinations.

detail.abstract: This paper is a practitioner's guide to agentic systems in quantitative investment research: what they are, how they should be built, and what a team must put in place before deploying them. A first wave of agentic systems has shown that agents can run the quantitative investment research process end to end. For deployment in production, however, research teams lack a standardised framework for using these systems safely and efficiently. Informed by a survey of 62 published agentic research systems, we derive a reference architecture from four stated conditions. It adapts a pattern established in the agent-systems literature, in which a system reasons in natural language and executes deterministically, and tailors it to quantitative research by defining where reasoning is needed and how much control each component requires. The result is two reasoning components, one designing the test and one reviewing the result, around a deterministic execution core, avoiding both over-generalised single agents and fragmented multi-agent designs. Building this requires redesigning research workflows around agent capabilities rather than mapping human processes onto agents step by step. A central concern is the balance between flexibility and control. Fixing the test design before any test is run, and counting every trial, preserves research integrity during delegated searches while still permitting genuine iteration. We further set out governance controls, principles for encoding research conventions as machine-readable skills, an illustrative readiness checklist, and the changing role and training of the researcher. Much of the critical preparation does not require autonomous agents and should be completed before deployment, giving research teams a practical roadmap towards agent-readiness.

detail.abstract: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, awarded to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, recognized that prices adjust slowly and at staggered intervals. Resorts offer a revealing setting for this idea, because they can leave a headline rate unchanged while adding mandatory fees. We pooled 574 online reviews of six resorts, from a value-tier family resort to Forbes Five-Star and Las Vegas casino resorts, matched to monthly STR market data. LIWC scored guests’ Achievement, Affiliation and Power language, and structural equation models related motives, ratings and class to perceived value and revenue. Guests judged value against one quality factor (β = .87), and every resort with reliable ratings showed a value gap: Value averaged 0.51 points below the other ratings. Unlike earlier evidence from mixed hotel samples, the gap widened with class, from −0.13 at the class 3 family resort to −0.65 at class 5 resorts (−0.26 per class step, t = −7.09), with Bellagio’s gap reaching −0.93. Guests at luxury resorts attributed the shortfall to resort fees, paid amenities and dated rooms. Within resorts, months of higher market ADR widened the gap (p ≈ .07). The Slutsky decomposition replicated: RevPAR raised ADR (β = .90) and occupancy restrained it (β = −.43). We argue that resort fees act as a flexible price layered on a sticky headline rate, and that guests charge the difference to value. Managers should fold mandatory fees into visible inclusions before raising rates. .

detail.abstract: Can "tik-tokenisation" in money and payments -where standardised financial claims are registered on shared platforms- constitute a new frontier? To reconcile such a question, this paper segregates tokenisation into its two components, namely through (1) the tokenisation of retail money: i.e. where issuers of retail means of payments (e.g. commercial banks) tokenise their liabilities toward non-banks (e.g. private citizens) and subsequently register them on shared platforms; and via (2) the tokenisation of FMIs: i.e. where the financial positions of FMIs (e.g. ACHs, CSDs, the central bank via its RTGS system) are recorded onto a shared platform. In the realm of tokenisation in the sphere of retail commercial bank money, it remains dubious to argue that tokenisation will constitute a new frontier, predominantly as tokenisation will likely bring about increased complexities, offer limited use-cases and may jeopardise financial stability. And while the tokenisation of FMIs offers greater potential towards the establishment of a new frontier, it will likely not reconcile issues in lengthy custodial chains in e.g. securities ownership. Finally, while the tokenisation of FMIs could amount to a new frontier, a separate question is if tokenisation should constitute a new frontier, as some of the claimed benefits of tokenisation could be brought about through other solutions without the imposition of additional complexities.

detail.abstract: This article identifies and describes the Stillwateroptions Staggered Collar™, an actively managed variant of the protective collar applied to individual high-volatility equities. The structure combines long stock, a long put struck near the purchase price, and a short call struck well above it. It is defined by the combination of a floor at or near cost, a wide band for gains, a high-volatility single-stock underlying, and the independent active management of each leg. We situate the structure against the Cboe S&P 500 95-110 Collar Index, the standard benchmark for passive collars, whose long-run record shows reduced volatility and crash losses at a substantial cost in return. We then contrast it with the bull call spread, its nearest lower-capital analogue, and argue that ownership of the underlying shares confers a management flexibility the spread lacks. Illustrations are drawn from a live account traded under the method beginning September 28, 2026. We also set out the costs and failure modes of the approach.

detail.abstract:
The start of the Middle East conflict in early 2026 caused an unprecedented drop in global petroleum supply. In response, oil prices jumped—but not to unprecedentedly high levels. The U.S. oil sector was a key factor in moderating the shock. For one, its steady increases in drilling helped create a large oversupply in the global market before the conflict, making it less of a challenge to offset the drop in Middle East oil output. In addition, U.S. commercial and government inventories were rapidly drawn down, filling half the gap between global supply and demand in the second quarter by some estimates. Inventories, though, are a limited resource and U.S. stockpiles stopped falling in July. As a consequence, the continued shortfall in global production has been managed by running down inventories in the rest of the world.

detail.abstract: Why do some acquirers consistently outperform others in mergers and acquisitions (M&A)? We propose a "win-to-win'' effect driven by endogenous information production. Specifically, information production following a high-return acquisition predicts higher abnormal returns in the acquirer’s subsequent deal. Accordingly, the commonly documented pattern of diminishing returns among serial acquirers is attenuated when the preceding transaction enhances the informativeness of the acquirer’s share price. This result is consistent with information and management contracting theories, which posit that improved information reduces agency frictions and relaxes financing constraints, thereby enhancing performance. Mechanism tests show that endogenous information production in prior deals improves stock liquidity and that the "win-to-win'' effect emerges only when the prior deal generates liquidity gains. The "win-to-win'' effect is stronger among acquirers that are better managed, less monitored, less unique, value (rather than growth) firms, and firms employing more data- or AI-oriented workers. Moreover, endogenous information production from the prior deal tempers the aggressive bidding behavior typically associated with prior success. Overall, our findings suggest that prior acquisition success translates into higher returns in subsequent deals when it stimulates information production.

detail.abstract: This paper asks whether a nominal macro anchor-the neutral real rate plus trend inflation-contains predictive information for government-bond excess returns. The direct long-yield gap is strong in sample but fails out of sample. The information survives when the anchor is embedded as the moving central tendency of a Hull-White-type Gaussian short-rate model and the predictive object is the observed yield minus the model's pure-expectations yield. On frozen US data from 1976 to 2026, the signal is positive but marginal for a 2-10 year basket and strong at ten years (zero-coupon 𝑅 2 OOS = 0.155, Clark-West 𝑡 = 3.12). Final-data tests show incremental content beyond the current ten-year yield (also for the future-price component) and beyond established bond-return predictors. Full-vintage ALFRED reconstruction leaves standalone CMT ten-year predictability essentially unchanged (𝑅 2 OOS = 0.0985 → 0.0986), but the CMT nested Clark-West statistic falls from 3.15 to 0.84; the stronger incremental claim is therefore not robust to the as-of reconstruction. Across nine developed markets, country-by-country predictive slopes are positive in all nine and recursive pseudo-out-of-sample 𝑅 2 is positive in six, while panel predictive regressions remain positive after country and month fixed effects (𝛽 = 0.0185, Driscoll-Kraay 𝑡 = 4.84) and after adding local yield-level and slope controls (𝛽 = 0.0134, 𝑡 = 3.08). An empirical-design decomposition shows that target construction, funding, sample length, and initialization materially affect headline results. The residual is deliberately labelled a model-implied term-premium signal rather than a structurally identified term premium.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether the relationship between average board age and corporate social responsibility (CSR) is nonlinear and whether product market competition conditions this relationship. Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory and stakeholder, agency, and institutional perspectives, we argue that increasing board age initially supports CSR through greater experience, stakeholder knowledge, and reputational awareness, but eventually constrains it as conservatism and risk aversion become more pronounced. Using 2,201 firm-year observations from 259 Vietnamese listed firms over 2015-2023, we estimate firm-and year-fixed-effects models and conduct extensive robustness and endogeneity analyses. The results reveal an inverted U-shaped relationship between board age and CSR. Because the estimated turning point is below the sample mean, most firms lie on the declining portion of the curve, producing a predominantly negative average association, especially for environmental and governance CSR. Product market competition serves as an important boundary condition: in less competitive industries (higher HHI), the negative effect associated with higher board age is weaker. The findings remain robust across alternative specifications, winsorized data, subgroup analyses, lagged models, fixed-effects instrumental-variable estimation, and two-step system GMM. By integrating a threshold-based account of board age with an external competitive boundary condition, this study explains when and why board demographics shape responsible corporate behavior in an emerging market.

detail.abstract: Fischer and Verrecchia (2000) study a reporting-bias model in which the market faces uncertainty over a manager's reporting incentives. They restrict attention to equilibria in which the price is linear in the report and show that there is only one such equilibrium. We show that it is the only equilibrium: no other price function is consistent with optimal reporting and Bayesian pricing. In contrast, earnings management models without incentive uncertainty admit a continuum of nonlinear separating equilibria and partially pooling equilibria. Our theorem implies that any positive amount of normally distributed incentive uncertainty, however small, eliminates them.

detail.abstract:
Romania taxes companies below a euro revenue ceiling at 1 to 3 percent of revenue
rather than 16 percent of profit, and the ceiling moved six times between 2013 and
2026. Each move supplies a counterfactual density at the notch from years when
the ceiling was elsewhere, and reassigns the same firms between a revenue base and
a profit base. In the accounts of every Romanian company, 9.6 million firm-years,
reported revenue piles up just below the ceiling and moves with it and with the
exchange rate. The excess is 2 to 8 percent of nearby firms. It comes mainly from
firms that gain from the regime, but loss-making firms bunch too, consistent with
a compliance cost of the profit tax. When the 2023 cut moved firms off the revenue
base, the mean reported margin fell by a sixth to over a quarter per firm that lost
eligibility, a result robust to the control band, attrition and the treatment of the
pre-period. When the 2018 increase moved firms onto it, margins rose by a tenth
to a quarter, but less robustly, and the effect fades after a year. Static estimates
therefore overstate the revenue from narrowing the regime, and most of the regime’s
cost sits with firms far below the ceiling, whose response is not observed.

detail.abstract: Australia has garnered significant recognition for its leadership in residential solar energy adoption, driven by incentive programs like the Feed-in Tariff and the Small-Scale Renewable Energy Scheme. Yet limited research has evaluated the policy's effects on residential solar photovoltaics in Australia. We thus examine how Feed-in tariff policies and different policy packages affect residential solar PV adoption using the quarterly data from July 2009 to June 2022. The benchmark results uncover that high Feed-in tariff rates, long-term contracts, and gross Feed-in tariff schemes substantially drive solar adoption in Australia. Still, the observed adverse relationship between cost and installed capacity highlights that upfront Small-Scale Renewable Energy Scheme subsidies effectively promote solar power. Our estimates may provide valuable implications for accelerating solar photovoltaic adoption and achieving renewable energy transitions in Australia. List of abbreviations.

detail.abstract: In 2025, changes to the USD 800 de minimis exemption coincided with a reported 54% decline in low-value parcels, motivating a computer-aided workflow for measuring firm-level policy exposure, survival risk, and employment adjustment.The computational workflow processes 21.8 million customs declarations (2016Q1-2026Q2) through hash-indexed enterprise matching and a four-dimensional firm-commodity-origin-quarter index, constructs quarterly feature matrices for 28,417 firms and approximately 714,000 firm-quarter observations, and integrates complementary log-log survival analysis with System GMM employment estimation.Batch calculation of quarterly exit hazards and recursive survival-probability updating yield a reported increase in annual exit probability from 8.4% to 11.1%, while the reported employment response is-6.9%. Rule-based stratification reports that firms with import-source concentration above 0.60 had 2.3 times the exit risk.Grouped computational summaries report that microenterprises accounted for 62% of exits but 24% of jobs, while estimated net employment declined by approximately 116,000 positions, 43% in logistics and warehousing. The reported survival rates are 74.3% and 51.8%; their eight-quarter interpretation and all numerical estimates require verification against source records and model diagnostics.

detail.abstract:
① Despite prolonged geopolitical tensions, including the U.S.–China rivalry and the Russia–Ukraine war, global trade has remained relatively stable, rather than fragmenting into full-scale rival blocs as seen during the Cold War(1947–90).
② Using UN General Assembly voting data, we measure how countries' relative proximity to the United States and China has shifted since 2017 along two dimensions: geopolitical(political and security) and geoeconomic(economic and development). The results reveal a decoupling between the two: while most countries have moved closer to the United States geopolitically, their geoeconomic alignment has shifted in varying directions across countries and regions. This divergence suggests that economic alignment is shaped by differences in countries’ industrial structures, external economic relations, and supply chain positions, rather than moving in tandem with political alignment.
③ “Connector countries,” closely integrated with both the U.S. market and China-centered production networks, help explain this resilience. Vietnam, India, and Mexico have sustained economic linkages through third-country production and sourcing as direct U.S.–China trade declines. Voting data show that these countries have moved closer to the United States geopolitically while remaining closer to China geoeconomically or shifting further toward it. This pattern offers a clue to their ability to maintain ties with both sides and, in doing so, supported global economic linkages.
④ Korea’s supply chains show similar changes. OECD Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) data for 2016–22 indicate that, of Korean value added embodied in exports to Vietnam, the share ultimately absorbed by U.S. final demand rose from 11.1% in 2016 to 18.5% in 2022, while China’s share increased from 7.3% to 13.9%.
The increases were particularly pronounced in computer, electronic and optical products, including semiconductors, where the shares rose from 12.8% to 21.0% for the United States and from 11.2% to 19.4% for China. Vietnam's production networks have thus become an increasingly important channel linking Korean value added to final demand in both markets.
⑤ The routes to U.S. final demand have also changed. The share of Korean value added reaching the United States directly remained broadly stable, at 73.1% in 2016 and 72.4% in 2022. By contrast, among indirect routes through third-country production bases, China’s share fell from 10.7% to 6.8%, while that of the ASEAN-5, including Vietnam, rose from 4.9% to 8.3%. In computer, electronic and optical products, including semiconductors, the ASEAN-5 share reached 18.6% in 2022, surpassing China’s 17.0%. ASEAN production networks are therefore playing a growing intermediary role, particularly in Korea’s key industries.
⑥ Taken together, these findings suggest that, despite recent geopolitical fragmentation, economic linkages across countries are being sustained through a reorganization of existing global supply chain pathways rather than severed. Korea, too, has maintained its connections with both the United States and China by leveraging established production networks in ASEAN, rather than sharply reducing ties with either side. By widening the range of production and export options available in the event of a geopolitical shock, this network structure may strengthen the resilience of Korea's supply chains.
⑦ However, greater reliance on ASEAN routes also creates risks. Tighter U.S. supply chain regulations — such as rules of origin or anti-circumvention investigations —could affect Korean firms and demand for Korean intermediate inputs through ASEAN production. Policy should preserve connector countries’ buffering role while managing the transmission of external policy changes and disruptions through these networks. Diversification across production bases and routes remains necessary.

detail.abstract: In 2023, a São Paulo appellate court affirmed a decision that had declared abusive the vote of a bank which, as the only creditor in its class, rejected a reorganization plan offering a seventy-five percent haircut paid over thirteen years. By disregarding the vote, the court confirmed the plan. No court asked whether the bank would receive under that plan at least what it would receive in liquidation. This Article uses that case to isolate a structural feature of Brazilian judicial reorganization that the comparative literature has not named: disregarding a dissenting creditor's vote has a constitutive effect. In Chapter 11, designation of a vote under section 1126(e) is subtractive. It removes a vote from the count and leaves the plan to face the best-interests test and the fair-and-equitable standard of section 1129. In Germany, the court does not inquire into the voter's motive at all and instead tests the result against the dissenter's position without the plan. Brazil's Law 11,101 of 2005, as amended in 2020, took the narrowest version of the American purpose test, limiting the annulment of votes to those "manifestly" cast to obtain an "unlawful advantage," and kept a cram-down provision that is purely arithmetic, with no best-interests test and no priority rule. Within that design, disregarding a dissenting vote is not a step toward confirmation. It is confirmation. The Article reconstructs the Brazilian regime, the American and German reference models, and the case law of the Superior Tribunal de Justiça. It shows that Brazilian courts have continued to apply the general abuse-of-rights standard of Article 187 of the Civil Code that the 2020 reform meant to displace, while the only guarantee a dissenting creditor has against expropriation is the court's view of its motives. The Article closes with an interpretive correction available to courts now and with draft statutory language that would make vote designation subtractive again.

detail.abstract:
Over the past decade, antitrust has enjoyed a resurgence as an alleged solution to the concentrated power of corporations, largely in response to the rise of Big Tech. Yet as a legal apparatus, antitrust reinforces the myth of "fair" and "competitive" capitalism in service to American Empire, capitalist accumulation, and environmental exploitation. This article challenges antitrust as a legitimate avenue for justice. It argues that modern antitrust was designed to stabilize capitalism in service to the American Empire. 

The article begins by providing an original inventory of views about society among modern antitrust's founding fathers based on primary and secondary sources. In doing so, it reveals antitrust's hidden origins in class war, white supremacy, sexism, xenophobia, colonialism, imperialism, ecocide, authoritarianism, and regulatory capture. Next, it reviews the imperialist and anti-labor foundations of prominent 20th century antitrust practitioners, embodied by figures like Louis Brandeis. The following section addresses the 21st century context, arguing that neo-Brandeisian antitrust advocates reproduce the socioeconomic injustices of the founders through the erasure of American Empire, structural harms inherent to capitalism, and the environmental crisis driven by unfettered accumulation and growth. The article concludes that antitrust is a false solution to corporate concentration which reinforces American Empire, socioeconomic inequality, and environmental breakdown inherent to the world-capitalist system. A rapid transition to ecosocialism is the best way forward for a just and sustainable future.

detail.abstract: This paper bridges market microstructure and derivatives pricing by introducing the Asymmetric Double Weibull (ADW) distribution to model extreme S&P 500 return increments under systemic shocks. Empirical evidence demonstrates a regime shift in the limit order book during systemic shocks, characterized by rapid directional liquidity exhaustion. We formalize this microstructural sparsity by establishing that the downside shape parameter strictly drops below unity, creating an infinite-activity pure-jump process, while the upside remains bounded. By analytically deriving the ADW tail risk parameters, we quantify the severity of these sub-exponential downside shocks, demonstrating how this asymmetric overdispersion renders continuous dynamic delta hedging structurally untenable and forces market makers to absorb unhedgeable exposure. Ultimately, the ADW framework provides a microstructural mechanism for the implied volatility skew observed in short-dated S&P 500 index put options.

detail.abstract: US Treasury securities serve as the key collateral for the international financial system, supporting repo transactions, derivatives clearing, and offshore dollar lending. This dissertation asks when and why US Treasuries' status as information-insensitive debt breaks down, specifically when foreign holders face unequal access to central bank liquidity, and what that failure means for the dollar's role as the world's reserve currency. The study extends the model of information-insensitive debt of Dang, Gorton, and Holmström (2015) to a setting where the collateral is issued through a single sovereign and held by agents on a global scale with unequal access to a lender of last resort. In this extension of the framework, agent B is divided into a domestic group that benefits from guaranteed access to central bank liquidity, and a foreign group that secures liquidity from a discretionary mechanism that fails with positive probability, and otherwise leads to liquidation of the assets at lower prices. Because for both agent types the value of trade is the same, the inequality in their participation gaps reduces to a single difference in their outside options. From this an interval of adverse signals follows, over which US Treasuries remain information-insensitive for domestic holders but become fragile for foreign ones, a split that stems from differences in institutional backing rather than any inherent characteristic of the collateral. The dissertation introduces two additional mechanisms, the absence of an alternative asset, which deepens the price impact of forced sales, and a fiscal-credibility mechanism that increases the wedge as the sovereign's fiscal condition deteriorates. By applying this framework to the March 2020 "dash for cash" turmoil the dissertation explains the pattern of foreign official Treasury sales and shows that the Federal Reserve's intervention aimed at mitigating the backstop shortfall, rather than opting for a structural change of the collateral itself. The dissertation further adds that the dollar's reserve role depends on a form of discretionary, unevenly shared, and gradually eroding institutional backstop.

detail.abstract: Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) are critical Internet infrastructures that facilitate local traffic exchange between Internet Service Providers (ISPs) through various peering arrangements. We posit that peering can significantly impact telecommunications costs and market outcomes. This paper examines the economic costs associated with peering compared to IP Transit services and analyzes their downstream effects on telecommunications markets globally. Using a comprehensive dataset combining publicly available peering port pricing data with proprietary IP Transit pricing information from 2019 to 2024, we demonstrate that peering costs are substantially lower than IP Transit costs by a large magnitude. Our analysis reveals that greater cost savings from peering are associated with lower broadband prices for consumers, expanded mobile network coverage, and increased overall telecommunications revenues. The links between transit-peering price differentials and positive market outcomes is particularly pronounced in moderately regulated economies and low-to lower-middle-income countries, suggesting that developing economies may derive greater benefits from IXP development. These findings have important policy implications, indicating that governments should consider supporting IXP growth and implementing policies that enable stakeholders to understand peering costs. Our study provides the first direct comparison of peering and IP Transit pricing while exploring the economy-wide implications of such decisions.

detail.abstract: Can a regulator use customer departures after a quality warning to tell whether a firm will improve its product? I study a firm that can cut costs by lowering quality at a fixed price. Customers leave when they notice deterioration and the gain from switching covers its cost. Two disclosure channels cause the same loss of customers at the firm's pre-intervention optimum: one reaches customers at random, while the other disproportionately reaches those who notice smaller cuts. The firm improves quality under the first channel but can cut it further under the second. What matters for its choice is how many customers it stands to lose on the next cut. In a separate comparison based on delivery costs, a regulator chooses where to spend a small budget; the relevant return per dollar therefore includes the value of the firm's quality response. When reach is sufficiently concentrated, that response can outweigh the gains to switchers and reduce consumer surplus even before delivery costs.

detail.abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic has increased the financial needs of health systems. It is unclear whether citizens who are willing to pay more also want the additional money to fund equal access, especially where a universal system coexists with privately financed tiers, as in Austria. Objective: I examine how willingness to accept higher taxes (WTA) and willingness to pay higher contributions to the public health system (WTP) relate to support for a one-tier health care system, and whether trust in public health care, household income, wealth and personal health moderate these relations. Methods: I use two waves of the Austrian Corona Panel Project (April 2021 and May 2022, totaling 2,202 observations of 1,545 respondents). Support for one-tier care is measured by a polychoric index of five statements. I estimate linear interaction models with cluster-robust standard errors, marginal effects across each moderator's range, within-between panel models and nine alternative specifications. Results: Each additional point of WTA is associated with 0.18 standard deviations (SD) less support for one-tier care, whereas WTP is unrelated to it on average. Both associations depend on trust and resources. Among people with low trust, few assets or poor health, the negative WTA slope is two to four times steeper than among people with high trust, more assets or good health. WTP is negatively associated with one-tier support among people in poor health, and the association turns positive with better health and, less robustly, with higher trust. The strongest supporters of one-tier care are those who reject higher taxes outright. Conclusions: Willingness to pay is not a reliable signal of solidarity. It coincides with support for equal access mainly among people who are able to contribute and who trust the public system. Reforms that ask for more money should therefore come with credible guarantees of equal access and efforts to build trust.

detail.abstract: Measures of labor market tightness (LMT) describe how difficult it is for firms to find workers. The labor market is considered tight if there are few job seekers available relative to job openings, implying stronger wage pressures as employers compete for scarce job seekers. Thus, good measures of LMT are important for predicting wage inflation and calibrating monetary policy. Recently, the hiring platform LinkedIn began producing three innovative LMT measures based on its user data. In this post, we use public data from the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) and the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) to evaluate the ability of these novel measures to predict wage and price inflation relative to existing LMT measures, finding that one stands out as particularly useful and timely.

detail.abstract: We examine talent reallocation following a private firm's transition to public equity markets. We explore this question using detailed employment and project-level data in the biopharmaceutical industry. We define a firm's peers at a precise level using overlap in project development portfolios based on therapeutic disease categories. Our results show that firms that go public significantly ramp up poaching of skilled labor from their still-private peers. Recruitment efforts are centered on scientists and high-experience workers, indicating that going public helps firms attract talented workers directly from their competitors. At the same time, recently-public firms exhibit an out-migration of less experienced labor to their still-private peers. This reallocation of talented agents to recently-public firms and away from competitors is reflected in project outcomes---recently-public firms that are successful in attracting talented agents exhibit stronger project development progress, while their private competitors experience worse progress. Our results illustrate the nature of labor reallocation following the transition to public equity markets at a granular level and provide a mechanism for the competitive advantages afforded to going-public firms.

detail.abstract: Focusing on productivity measurement, this article contributes to the growth and development accounting literature by improving the accuracy of results within the existing framework-without introducing new variables. We implement three simultaneous revisions to the standard growth and development accounting frameworks: (i) accounting for labor quality, (ii) allowing for time-and country-varying factor elasticities, and (iii) relaxing the assumption of constant unitary returns to scale. All affect the contributions to growth and development. Using data from PWT 10.0, we calibrate growth and development accounting frameworks to quantify and rank the drivers of growth and development across 130 countries from 1990 to 2019. Results and stylized facts are presented at the country level, by income group, and for the full sample. The three proposed refinements, pedagogically grounded in empirical evidence, provide more precise estimates of the contributions of capital, labor, labor quality, and aggregate productivity to economic growth and development.

detail.abstract: We examine how firms respond to changing social and political pressures by studying their DEI activities following the murder of George Floyd in May 2020 and the subsequent rise of anti-DEI legislation and political backlash during 2023-2025. Using BERT-based textual analysis of proxy statements, we measure firms' substantive DEI-related commitments, including board and executive team diversity, workforce DEI initiatives, and financial commitments. Disclosed DEI investment follows a rollercoaster pattern, increasing sharply from 2020-2022 and decreasing just as sharply from 2023-2025. The rise and subsequent decline are concentrated among the same firms: those with high pre-existing DEI engagement, high public visibility, and strong ties to pro-DEI investors, customers, and employees. As a result, cross-sectional dispersion in DEI investment first widens and then compresses, falling below its pre-2020 level by 2025. These patterns are difficult to reconcile with a simple stakeholder-demand view in which firms with pro-DEI stakeholders persistently maintain high DEI investment. Instead, the influence of stakeholder demand on corporate social investment depends critically on the political environment, and stakeholder-oriented corporate policies can be less stable than evidence from a single political environment would suggest.

detail.abstract: Congress is supposed to be the central engine of legitimacy within the U.S. constitutional system, but lately its capacity to perform this function has declined. This brief symposium essay speculates about the causes and implications of this change. It posits, first, that checks and balances within the U.S. constitutional system are not only limiting but also empowering, as they enable more legitimate and thus effective government. It further suggests that Congress should be first among equals in this process; it should play the central role in promoting public acceptance of federal laws and policies. Changes in media, society, and politics, however, have impaired Congress's capacity to perform this function, and there is reason to fear that these changes are deep-seated, as they are producing similar effects in other democracies with different constitutional arrangements. The essay suggests two potential responses. First, courts and Congress itself should strengthen Congress's "reactive" powers over funding and oversight so that Congress can at least respond effectively to executive initiatives. Second, courts should take care to preserve their own checking function by favoring politically symmetric constitutional doctrines over unduly partisan ones.

detail.abstract: Displayed depth can return near a new quote without replenishing earlier prices, and a first return to a depth threshold need not persist to a later endpoint. We quantify these distinctions in a repeatedly used Nasdaq single-venue pre-market development sample from January–March 2026. For 286,862 paired origins on 51 dates, fifteen-second normalized shortfall averages about 0.0208 at fixed prices and 0.0108 at moving quotes. This difference coexists with equal measurements on 94.04% of the original parent weight; definite reversals occupy 1.48%. On a linked set of 135,929 initially short one-second landmarks over 34 dates, compatible first returns occupy only about 1.45% of risk weight. Of that small return mass, 29.94–30.37% is short again at the endpoint. Returns are defined on the completed-event path after merging equal receive timestamps. A supporting quantity–occupation comparison has a mean absolute discrepancy of about 0.004; its large no-crossing contribution primarily reflects the prevalence of such paths. Observation envelopes retain unknown paths; they do not provide sampling confidence or independent confirmation. The results concern short-window displayed-depth measurement relative to specified reference quantities, without identifying announcement effects or execution profitability.

detail.abstract: This appendix proposes a broad luxury tax as a new own EU resource, bundled with the abolition of VAT refunds for non-EU that would also generate additional revenue for member states, mostly from personal (portable) luxury goods. Both components are motivated by the finding that raising revenue via luxury taxation generates a significantly lower marginal economic burden than other taxes. Indeed, luxury taxation is justified on the grounds of status externalities and progressivity, and it taxes the wealthiest without deterring investments nor philanthropy. However, national luxury taxation is currently distorted downward due to international tax competition. In the case of portable luxury goods there is tax competition for internationally mobile shoppers and in the case of residence-based luxury goods (e.g. cars) there is tax competition for high-net-worth residents. We therefore propose to implement a new own EU resource as a luxury excise on values exceeding category-specific per-item price thresholds. We propose a uniform ad valorem rate across categories as a focal point to facilitate negotiations. Economic modeling suggests that an EU-wide additive luxury tax rate of 20% is justified on the grounds of status externalities and signaling alone, while socially optimal tax rates are likely substantially higher once progressivity benefits are taken into account. A 20% rate is estimated to raise EUR 42 billion per year for the EU budget. While a luxury tax restricted to any particular product category would create uneven relative burdens across member states, our broad product scope (covering yachts, luxury vehicles, personal luxury items, hospitality, and fine spirits) achieves a more balanced burden relative to GDP. Countries collecting higher revenue shares (e.g., France, Italy, Spain) would benefit disproportionately from the concurrent abolition of VAT refunds, which is estimated to raise up to EUR 4 billion EU-wide. This combined reform is feasible, highly progressive, and politically viable.

detail.abstract:
While the EU looks for new own resources to repay the debt contracted during Covid, this appendix argues that wealth taxation can work if designed well. The proposal deliberately avoids the pitfalls that have historically undermined recurrent wealth taxes. It is a one-off levy, assessed on the net wealth each resident holds on a single past reference date (1 January 2027), and paid over thirty years at low annual rates. In the Central scenario, yearly marginal rates are 0.1% on wealth between EUR 1 and 10 million, 0.3% between EUR 10 and 100 million, and 0.5% above EUR 100 million. We also present an alternative scenario where the tax only applies above EUR 100 million. 

Because the base is fixed in the past, the levy is a lump sum in the economic sense: no decision taken after 2026, whether to invest, to found a company or to emigrate, can change what is owed, so the tax does not distort future accumulation and activity. The low annual rates keep the tax non-confiscatory and comfortably within constitutional bounds. Liquidity is addressed head-on: payment is reduced if a taxpayer’s wealth drops and the taxpayer may pay in company shares. Finally, a Deferral Account secures the claim against emigration and death. 

Built this way, the tax would raise about EUR 26 billion a year, close to EUR 790 billion (that is 4.5% of EU GDP) over the thirty-year horizon. The proposal adopts the low-rate one-off logic of Pisani-Ferry & Mahfouz (2023), who recommended an exceptional levy of 5% of GDP spread over thirty years to finance the climate transition. Besides, it adapts the deferral and one-off mechanisms designed for the Californian 2026 Billionaire Tax Act initiative (Proponents of California Initiative 25-0024, 2025). 

The instrument rests on solid economic foundations. Farhi (2010) shows that a one-off capital levy is the efficient response to a negative fiscal shock, precisely the case created by the pandemic-era debt, the security build-up and the financing of the transition. Progressive wealth taxation is independently justified on distributive grounds: Saez & Zucman (2019) argue that it is the most appropriate tool for restoring progressivity at the very top, since the ultra-wealthy report little taxable income. 

The tax revenue could simply be paid into the EU budget as an own resource, or used to repay the common debt, and we show that it works well on those terms. Alternatively to this default revenue use, we also argue for another strategic use. Rather than shrink the Union’s balance sheet by repaying the debt, the proceeds could endow a European sovereign fund, at a time when major investments are needed for the ecological transition and for competitiveness. 

The combination of low annual rates, deferral, payment in kind and asset-backed recovery is what makes the tax simultaneously enforceable, non-distortive and respectful of taxpayers’ liquidity constraints and asset control. We believe such a tax can actually be adopted. It does not interact with the taxes Member States already levy; it raises real revenue; it is constitutional in every EU jurisdiction; it rests on solid economic and democratic foundations; and it is increasingly on the political agenda.

detail.abstract: Rough stochastic volatility models reproduce the steep short-maturity implied-volatility skew, with the Hurst exponent H controlling the roughness of the volatility path. We ask whether H can be identified from the object one actually calibrates to—an implied-volatility surface—via a calibration audit of the rough Heston model from synthetic known-answer surfaces to two live cryptocurrency options markets. First, a single maturity cannot identify H: the inverse problem pins the variance level, skew and volatility-of-volatility, but H is the flat eigen-direction, degenerate with the volatility-of-volatility and corrupted by a tenth of a volatility point of quote noise. Second, the multi-maturity surface mitigates but does not cure this: the skew term structure tightens H by roughly an order of magnitude at clean data, yet the degeneracy persists and returns under realistic noise. Third, on a live Deribit Bitcoin surface H is non-identifiable outright: it rails to its boundary, is strongly correlated with the volatility-of-volatility, and two equally good fits land at different parameters. This non-identification is intrinsic—a structural H–volatility-of-volatility degeneracy—not a span artefact: a maturity-adapted Riccati resolution makes the full one-year span computable, identifiability is unchanged, and the longest tenor is the least H-informative. Both findings replicate on Ethereum. This is the option-calibration counterpart of the observational equivalence documented for roughness estimation from realised variance. Separately, the model fits the gross crypto smile to within about a volatility point but systematically under-produces the crash-fear put tail on both markets, even at maximal roughness. All machinery is validated against the model's characteristic function.

detail.abstract: Why is it that two borrowers who look much alike can be offered very different rates when applying for a credit card? detail.abstract: We study the random assignment of objects when agents may prefer remaining unassigned to receiving some objects. detail.abstract:
Critical infrastructure security depends on the maturity of the state and local cyber-physical systems (CPS) workforce. As telecommunications, water, energy, public health, and transportation facilities adopt Internet-of-Things (IoT) and operational technologies (OT), the security of these systems underpins the national supply chain, communications, disaster response, and access to basic services such as water, electricity and heat, and much of it is managed at the state level. Variation in workforce capacity across states therefore becomes a determinant of national resilience and of the security of critical digital infrastructure. 

            This article presents an exploratory, state-level study of how workforce capacity relates to infrastructure need across the United States, with particular attention to telecommunications. The research team built a state-year panel covering the 50 states and the District of Columbia from 2010 through 2024, drawing on the U.S. Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and the Bureau of Economic Analysis. The analysis is descriptive.

            Results of this pilot study suggest that telecommunications specialization is positively associated with measured capacity, while utilities specialization is negatively associated with it. Notably, four states (Arkansas, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and West Virginia) combine low measured capacity with high relative need under every definition tested. The patterns found in this study frame telecommunications resilience as a cross-sector workforce problem rather than a telecommunication sector specific issue. The article documents the absence of a federal statistical product isolating CPS and OT roles. The article also offers recommendations for state and federal interventions as well as an ongoing research direction.

detail.abstract: Heat negatively affects labor supply and worker productivity, especially in physically demanding jobs that occur outdoors and in non-climate-controlled environments, yet evidence remains limited in sub-Saharan Africa. Using data from three harvest seasons at a sugarcane estate in Ethiopia, we exploit plausibly exogenous day-today temperature variations to estimate the impact of high daily temperatures on worker absence on the following day. We find that a 1°C increase in daily temperature increases absences by approximately 3 percent. Allowing for nonlinear temperature effects reveals that absences only increase when daily average temperatures exceed 23°C or daily maximum temperatures exceed 30°C. Worker absences induced by days with average temperatures above 23°C correspond to 133,000 meters of forgone workerequivalent output and 140,000 Ethiopian birr in worker earnings. Given the expected increases in extreme heat, these findings underscore the need for adaptation measures to protect workers and sustain agricultural production in sub-Saharan Africa.

detail.abstract: We provide causal evidence that cash holdings shape retail investors' disposition effect. Identification comes from quasi-random variation in the intraday timing of cash arrival resulting from earlier mutual fund redemptions. Consistent with the two-layered mental accounting model of Dai, Qin, and Wang (2026, Journal of Finance), investors receiving the cash shock exhibit a significantly weaker disposition effect in their stock trading. The effect operates almost entirely through increased loss realization, with gain realization largely unchanged. It also extends to deep-loss positions: cash-rich investors sell deep losers outright, while cash-poor investors sell only after prices rebound. The effects persist among investors facing weak liquidity constraints and concentrate among those who actively monitor their portfolio budgets. Holding more cash also improves the performance of selling decisions. Cash gives investors the psychological room to admit mistakes and start afresh.

detail.abstract: Causal mediation analysis decomposes a treatment effect into indirect pathways through mediators and direct pathways through other processes. Tabular foundation models perform classification and regression through in-context learning, providing estimates of conditional means and propensity scores used in causal mediation analysis. Constructing confidence intervals from these estimates requires accounting for uncertainty introduced by fitting and combining several nuisance functions. We introduce MediPFN, an amortized inference framework that adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to nuisance prediction and combines its predictions through a cross-fitted influence-function estimator. A separate head learns quantiles of the estimator's standardized error from simulated tables with known indirect effects. Supervised fine-tuning, symmetrization, and independent calibration then produce a confidence interval. We establish coverage bounds for the resulting intervals under standard assumptions. Across experiments, MediPFN attains coverage closer to the nominal level than several comparators. It also reduces the computational cost of uncertainty quantification, running 59.1 times faster than bootstrap in matched comparisons.

detail.abstract: Physiological artifacts and inter-participant variability complicate electroencephalography (EEG) decoding. This study examines whether exposure to recorded artifacts during reconstruction pretraining improves 200-class cross-subject visual EEG classification. PhysioMotion artifact segments are aligned with a full-channel THINGS-EEG2 derivative and added through mixing with a controlled signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). A Macaron Conformer is pre-trained and then fine-tuned on uncontaminated visual EEG. An exploratory sweep examines seven exposure proportions. The main ablation study compares P25, which exposes 25% of pre-training windows, with Clean, P25-Mask, and P25-Gauss. These variants remove artifact exposure and region weighting, remove waveform injection alone, or replace recorded artifacts with power-matched Gaussian noise, respectively. Each condition is repeated with three seeds in ten participant-held-out folds, using nine participants for training in each fold. P25 achieves 8.73% mean uncontaminated Top-1 accuracy, compared with 7.86% for Clean, 7.23% for P25-Mask, and 8.03% for P25-Gauss. The contamination test covers all ten participants. P25 exceeds Clean in seed-averaged accuracy for every participant at all six contamination rates and ranks highest among the four conditions for nine participants at every rate. Under full-window contamination, P25 reaches 7.79%, exceeding Clean, P25-Mask, and P25-Gauss by 0.66, 1.22, and 0.62 percentage points. Finally, this study proposes linear probes, Integrated Gradients maps and t-SNE graphs for comprehensive analysis and attribution. Overall, the results support a contribution from recorded artifact waveforms within this pre-training framework. The advantage under contamination reflects higher absolute decoding accuracy since the average decline from uncontaminated performance is not reduced.

detail.abstract: We study nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type processes and propose an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. Under mild conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show that the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Under stationarity and mixing conditions, we establish the same rate for recursion-map estimation and derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian quasi-likelihood (QLIKE) loss. The convergence rates depend on the true lag orders and remain unchanged when the fitted orders are overspecified. detail.abstract: As climate change becomes an ever more pressing issue, adaptation policies are increasingly important. However, one issue that has been raised is "maladaptation" due to a lack of long-term perspective, inclusivity, and cross-sectoral collaboration. The purpose of this study was to investigate whether introducing the perspective of "Imaginary Future Generations" (IFGs), which has been shown to generate futurability in individuals, could be effective in terms of generating long-term perspective, inclusivity, and cross-sectoral collaboration in an integrated discussion practice about climate change mitigation and adaptation measures by policymakers. Specifically, we held deliberation practice workshops with municipal officials in Mito City in Japan, looking at formulating and evaluating climate change mitigation and adaptation measures with a view to society in 2060. We compared the discussion details and results between when participants took the perspective of current generations and when they took that of IFGs. From this comparison, we found that introducing the IFG perspective resulted in participants tending to suggest policies placing greater emphasis on residents' participation, and that elements related to inclusivity and cross-sectoral collaboration were observed in the proposals. From the questionnaire survey administered to the participants, we also found that adopting the IFG perspective was shown to change participants' perceptions toward measures like mass relocation such that they were more likely to prioritize measures necessary in the long term, regardless of cost. Together, these findings indicate that incorporating the IFG framework to generate futurability may increase long-term perspective, inclusivity, and cross-sectoral collaboration when formulating adaptation policies.
