detail.abstract:
1. We examine youth employment trends amid AI diffusion using National Pension subscriber data and the Economically Active Population Survey. First, the decline in youth employment remains concentrated in industries with high AI exposure. Between June 2022 and June 2026, youth employment fell by 285,000, with high-exposure industries accounting for 268,000, or 94%, of the decline. Sharp declines occurred in information services (-31.4%), publishing (-27.4%), computer programming (-16.6%) and professional services (-11.6%). Employment among workers in their 50s continued to rise in these same industries. This pattern is consistent with the persistence of the “seniority-biased technological change” documented by Han and Oh (2025).

2. Second, youth employment has declined less in industries where AI is used to augment human work. Industries with a higher share of AI use for automation saw larger declines in youth employment. No comparable pattern emerged for augmentation, where AI assists rather than replaces human work. These findings suggest that AI’s employment effects may depend on how it is used, not simply on whether it is adopted.

3. Third, unemployment has risen more among young university graduates, who tend to be more exposed to AI. Since November 2022, the unemployment rate has averaged 7.0% among young people with a bachelor’s degree or higher, compared with 5.4% among those without one—a gap of 1.6 percentage points. Before then, the two groups had similar unemployment rates.

4. Fourth, the decline in youth employment reflects not only reduced hiring but also increased exits from employment. More young workers leaving high-exposure industries have also entered unemployment. The challenge therefore extends beyond finding a first job: young workers may also face greater difficulty staying employed and accumulating experience and skills.

5. These patterns do not establish that AI caused the recent weakness in youth employment. The reversal of pandemic-era over-hiring, a growing preference for experienced hires, weaker in-house training and the spread of remote work may all have contributed. Rather than acting as a standalone shock, AI may be accelerating pre-existing changes in hiring and work practices.

6. The recent decline need not imply a persistently weaker employment outlook for young people. Their active use of AI and ability to adapt to new technologies could make them major beneficiaries of productivity gains and new jobs over time. Policy should focus on rebuilding career ladders rather than preserving existing entry-level jobs, enabling young workers to gain experience and skills while working with AI. Priorities include work-based apprenticeships, support for firms’ investment in training and mentoring, and a review of whether policy incentives strike an appropriate balance between investment in technology and human capital.

detail.abstract: We conduct a broad investigation of whether nontraded factors price the cross-section of returns, accounting for weak identification and global model misspecification. We collect 102 nontraded factors from 51 papers in mainstream finance and economics journals and replicate 145 published specifications using widely used test portfolios. Because these factors are often weakly correlated with asset returns and their models are likely misspecified, conventional risk-premium tests may overstate their pricing ability. Standard econometric methods classify up to 39% as priced, whereas robust procedures reduce that share to 4%-13%; multiple-testing adjustments weaken the evidence, and adding the market factor worsens identification. Complementary beta-sorted portfolio analysis provides similar results: only 11.2% of long-short strategies earn statistically significant average returns, with small premia. Our results do not necessarily imply that nontraded factors are unpriced, but most published proxies receive little support from robust pricing tests or portfolio sorts immune to weak identification.

detail.abstract: Remittances to Africa reached $124.2 billion in 2025, yet sending money to the continent remains the most expensive in the world. I estimate how much African families lose in fees each year and what reform to the UN targets of 3% and 5% would return, combining 2025 inflows and average costs for 43 countries from IFAD with World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide data for the third quarter of 2025. Weighting each country's cost by the money it receives, families lose at least $5.2 billion a year, or 4.2% of inflows. Using regional averages instead gives $8.3 billion, and counting bank channels would raise the bill further. Reaching the 3% goal would return between $1.6 billion and $4.6 billion a year. Cost falls sharply with market size: across 33 countries a tenfold rise in inflows is associated with a 4.3 percentage point fall in cost (R² = 0.40). Ten countries account for three quarters of the gain from reform, and routes between African countries cost up to 13 times more than diaspora routes. I conclude that reform should target a small set of large markets, hot-spot corridors and bank-based channels, not regional averages.

detail.abstract: We propose the Complex Market Hypothesis: substantial return predictability arises from many individually weak signals. We model a computational arms race in which investors choose model scale and learn from limited data. Random matrix theory yields an essentially unique linear equilibrium and characterizes the distribution of model sizes. Prices transmit information from larger models to smaller ones, allowing both to coexist. Cheaper computation can raise aggregate spending and widen performance gaps across funds. Even when every investor observes all signals determining payoffs, uncertainty about their predictive coefficients sustains a sizable equity premium.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether a crowdfunded, behavior-linked matched savings program can improve saving consistency and strengthen financial identity among formerly incarcerated individuals during reintegration. Reintegration is often evaluated through employment, housing, and recidivism, yet stable income does not automatically become financial stability. Formerly incarcerated individuals may face irregular income, stigma, family obligations, unexpected expenses, and reduced self-efficacy, all of which can make saving difficult even when employment and basic financial knowledge are present (Goffman, 1963; Pager, 2003; Mani et al., 2013; Montes et al., 2021; Bandura, 1997). The pilot began in August 2026 and currently involves 40 participants enrolled in the Restart Program, the reintegration initiative run by the Thailand Institute of Justice (TIJ). Over roughly 90 days, participants complete six saving cycles linked to biweekly income. The intervention combines five elements: financial literacy, a 1:1 savings match funded through Taejai crowdfunding, a limited emergency safety net, milestone recognition and social encouragement, and a passport-style tracking tool that records saving intentions, actual saving, income, necessary expenses, and progress toward a self-defined goal. Using an exploratory single-group mixed-methods design, the study combines pre- and post-intervention surveys, verified savings records, passport data, and short-answer or interview responses. The primary outcomes are saving consistency and changes in financial self-efficacy and financial identity. Preliminary savings records show that participants collectively saved 90% of their combined target amount during three reported saving cycles. Early focus-group discussions suggest emerging behavioral changes, with some participants reporting that they had begun setting savings targets and prioritizing saving before spending. Others described discovering an ability to save that they had previously doubted. These observations suggest early engagement with structured saving and possible shifts in perceived financial capability, although sustained saving consistency and changes in financial identity remain to be evaluated. This manuscript presents interim findings from an ongoing intervention, with final outcome data expected on November 15, 2026. Three exploratory hypotheses guide the study: (H1) saving consistency and goal attainment improve across intervention cycles; (H2) financial self-efficacy and financial identity strengthen between baseline and endline; and (H3) greater saving consistency is associated with larger improvements in both outcomes. Final analysis will evaluate these hypotheses, although the single-group design and short observation period limit causal inference and conclusions about lasting behavioral change.

detail.abstract:
Deploying econometric time-deformation and cross-asset covariance estimators into continuous 24/7 autonomous trading systems exposes three severe operational failure modes that remain unobserved in offline historical backtests: (1) Subordinated Volume-Clock Liveness Deadlock, wherein replacing chronological wall-clock bars with pure volume-threshold sampling (Clark, 1973; Lopez de Prado, 2018) causes the bar generator to stall indefinitely during intraday liquidity vacuums, blinding downstream risk and stop-loss engines to accumulating macroeconomic shocks; (2) Spectral Indefiniteness in Asynchronous Cross-Market Covariance, where applying the Hayashi-Yoshida (2005) overlap estimator across non-synchronously traded global assets (US equities, Tokyo Stock Exchange equities, spot FX, and precious metals futures) eliminates the Epps (1979) downward correlation bias but frequently yields symmetric matrices with strictly negative eigenvalues (lambda_min < 0) that crash inverse-variance risk parity solvers; and (3) Discrete Exchange Microstructure Quantization Violation, where continuous-share Half-Kelly optimization violates tiered tick-size tables and mandatory 100-share board-lot constraints on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE).

Completing the mathematical trilogy established in Hashimoto (2026a, 2026b), we formulate a unified temporal and cross-asset econometric architecture implemented in the open-source lumina-quant library. First, we introduce a Timeout-Bounded Subordinated Volume Clock tau_k = min(tau_vol, tau_prev + dt_max) (dt_max = 1,800 s) that restores return Gaussianity (reducing excess kurtosis by 78.1%) while mathematically guaranteeing worst-case heartbeat liveness. Second, we construct a Higham-Projected Hayashi-Yoshida Lead-Lag Operator that maps asynchronous tick-overlap covariance matrices onto the nearest Positive Semi-Definite (PSD) cone via alternating Dykstra projections, guaranteeing lambda_min >= 0 and zero matrix-inversion crashes. Third, we derive a closed-form Discrete Exchange Tick-and-Lot Conformance Operator paired with a 3.63 ns cache-resident Rust Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) execution sentinel. Empirical evaluation across 5 years of multi-market data (2021-2026) and offline unit verification confirms 0.0% liveness deadlocks, 0.0% PSD solver failures, and 0.0% exchange order rejections.

detail.abstract: This paper examines cohesion, which reflects the semantic relations that integrate successive information units into a unified narrative. Cohesion in analyst reports is higher for experienced and historically accurate analysts but declines under cognitive constraints. More cohesive reports generate 10.2% more abnormal trading volume per quartile increase in cohesion, and the effect strengthens when information uncertainty is high, textual content is complex, or the analyst issues a bold or negative opinion. Firms covered by more cohesive reports subsequently experience lower return volatility and bid-ask spreads, indicating improved information dissemination. Although the average cohesion declines after the popularization of generative artificial intelligence, investors continue to value human-crafted narrative integration. Overall, cohesion reduces the cost of processing narrative information and improves capital market efficiency.

detail.abstract: Delegating work to an AI agent also delegates decisions about what to look up, how long to think, and how much to double-check. We study whether these decisions are economically rational and whether they are aligned with task performance. In our augmented revealed-preference experiment, five open-weight language models repeatedly allocate fixed budgets across worked examples, deliberation, and verification under varied resource costs, subsequently solving reasoning tasks using their selected resources. A separate calibration measures the performance of every possible allocation, so the same choices can be tested for both rationality and alignment. The models' choices demonstrate robust preference consistency across nearly all tasks, yet this coherence collapses when preferences are required to align with performance. To uncover the root of this misalignment, we evaluate parametric assumptions for both agents' preferences and production technology. We find that, while revealed utility is near-homothetic, the true production function is governed by a step-threshold in deliberation and non-monotonic returns in verification, inducing the observed mismatch and inefficient use of computational resources.

detail.abstract:
Quantitative trading engines rely predominantly on finite historical backtests and stochastic Monte Carlo simulations to validate execution and risk-sizing code. However, finite sample paths leave uncountable state-space regions—such as odd-lot discrete integer truncations, adverse fill slippage during scale-in pyramiding, and exception-masked SQLite schema drift—untested prior to live deployment. In this fourth installment of the Lumina Capital research series, extending the execution-cost governance framework of Hashimoto (2026a), the multi-chamber dynamic leverage boundaries of Hashimoto (2026b), and the timeout-bounded asynchronous econometrics of Hashimoto (2026c), we introduce a four-stage formal verification and regime-conditioned execution architecture.

First, we formulate a Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) verification framework using the Microsoft Z3 Theorem Prover over linear real and integer arithmetic (QF_LIRA), proving that six core execution invariants—discrete lot sizing bounds, slippage-proof pyramiding stop synchronization, risk-unit (R-multiple) sign symmetry, drawdown brake monotonicity, prop-firm lot consistency smoothing, and static SQL Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) schema parity—are strictly unsatisfiable under negation (not I_safety => UNSAT), guaranteeing zero mathematical counterexamples across the unbounded price-quantity domain.

Second, we establish the Friday Afternoon Cross-Asset Exit Divergence Theorem: after 11:00 ET on Fridays, institutional T+1 balance-sheet de-risking induces negative drift in US equities (mu_eq < 0), whereas weekend geopolitical hedge accumulation induces positive drift in spot gold (mu_Au > 0). Across 1,254 trading days (2021-2026), tightening the trailing stop multiplier from 1.00x to 0.75x on Fridays after 11:00 ET improves US equity returns by +0.41R, whereas applying the same tightening to gold degrades returns by -1.08R—a 1.49R cross-asset divergence (p < 0.001).

Third, we derive a cross-sectional Opening Range Compression Gate (Median ORB_30m < 0.75%) that eliminates morning bid-ask chop while preserving 100% of genuine institutional breakout trends (RVOL_open >= 1.50).

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether changes in India's capital gains tax regime affected monthly foreign portfolio equity inflows between 1997 and 2024. While global risk conditions and domestic financial factors are well-established determinants of cross-border capital flows, the role of capital gains taxation remains empirically unclear. Using an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework with regime-specific tax dummies, the study evaluates whether tax reforms influence both the level of inflows and their sensitivity to global financial risk, proxied by the VIX. A GARCH (1,1) specification is employed to account for time-varying volatility in flows. The results indicate that the 2004 abolition of capital gains tax is associated with higher average inflows. Interaction terms suggest some variation in risk sensitivity across tax regimes, but rolling estimates point to gradual rather than discrete changes in coefficients. Stability diagnostics provide mixed evidence: while CUSUM tests do not reject parameter stability in mean relationships, CUSUM-squared statistics indicate significant instability in higher-order moments, consistent with time-varying volatility rather than structural breaks in conditional means. These patterns align more closely with evolving global financial conditions, including the Global Financial Crisis, than with discrete tax-induced regime shifts. Overall, the evidence suggests that capital gains tax changes are associated with inflow dynamics but do not constitute clear structural breaks in mean behavioral relationships. Instead, instability appears to operate primarily through volatility dynamics and broader global financial cycles rather than shifts in underlying tax sensitivity.

detail.abstract: Banks hold diversified credit portfolios, yet capital rules assess each exposure separately. Separate assessment favors holding loans through nonbank lenders, where surpluses on performing loans offset shortfalls on others and justify a lower charge. We show that Basel's internal ratings-based rules lower the charge further. Their single-firm calibration assigns borrower-specific risk that pooling has largely removed, understating the default probability of the bank's claim in aggregate stress. At nine major U.S. bank holding companies, a charge computed from the nonbank lenders' underlying loans would raise required capital by $160.4 billion in 2024Q3, or 14.6% of combined Tier 1 capital, after accounting for the standardized requirement. The U.S. correlation multiplier for financial counterparties and Basel III's supervisory loss given default each close less than a tenth of the gap. When capital constraints bind, the undercharge supports more lending and larger losses in aggregate stress relative to equity. Consistent with financing responding to capital requirements, foreign banks' U.S. branches reduce financing of nonbank lenders by about 12% after home-country capital reforms, relative to branches whose home rules remain unchanged.

detail.abstract: Labor-related disruptions can propagate across firm boundaries, yet little is known about whether institutional labor protections can stabilize supply chain relationships. Using 26,723 supplier-customer pair-year observations from 2005 to 2019 and the staggered adoption of state-level paid sick leave mandates in the United States, we examine how labor protection affects relationship continuity and customer purchases. Difference-indifferences estimates show that paid sick leave mandates reduce relationship termination by 2.7 percentage points, an approximately 15.2% decline relative to the sample mean. Customers also increase purchases from suppliers subject to these mandates within existing relationships, and the result remains significant when comparing suppliers serving the same customer in the same year. The findings are robust to alternative staggered-adoption estimators, comparison groups, adjustments for the customer disclosure threshold, treatment measures, fixed-effects specifications, and placebo assignments. Mechanism analyses support two complementary channels. Paid sick leave improves operational resilience by stabilizing employment, raising labor and total factor productivity, and reducing supply-demand mismatches. It also strengthens relational governance by reducing labor-related legal exposure and improving health-and-safety, working-condition, and product-quality outcomes. The stabilizing effect is concentrated among suppliers facing greater operational vulnerability and in relationships characterized by greater relational frictions. These findings show that institutional labor protection can shape interfirm exchange and suggest that labor protection can function as an institutional form of supply-chain insurance. For supply chain managers, suppliers' labor protection conditions can therefore inform supplier risk assessment and procurement decisions.

detail.abstract: The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act establishes a federal framework for payment stablecoin issuers and subjects them to the Bank Secrecy Act. It requires technical capabilities to block, freeze, and reject impermissible transactions, and the technological capability to comply with lawful orders to seize, freeze, burn, or prevent the transfer of payment stablecoins. The statute specifies these requirements functionally; the engineering architecture remains open: where controls are evaluated, who may trigger them, how compliance authority is protected against compromise, and how each action is made verifiable. We argue that compliance authority is among the most privileged capabilities in a stablecoin system and should be protected at least as strongly as mint authority. We (i) derive eight engineering control objectives (CO-1 to CO-8) and map statutory verbs to ledger state-transition semantics; (ii) define a threat model with seven adversary classes, including administrative-key theft, insider abuse, and forged legal orders; (iii) present a layered reference architecture with two-phase enforcement (a reversible hold must precede any irreversible seizure or burn), threshold (M-of-N) authorization, and cross-chain containment based on issuer-controlled burn-and-mint bridging (ERC-7281); and (iv) implement the on-ledger layer, an asymmetric quorum authority, issuer-controlled bridging, and a sanctions-list ingestion tool, prove five token invariants, the token side of a sixth (quorum) invariant, and seven authority properties by symbolic execution over arbitrary contract states (signature recovery is abstracted and covered by tests), and measure gas cost. Packing compliance state into the balance slot keeps transfer overhead at 3.1% (1,054 gas) regardless of the number of active holds, while a 2-of-N signature quorum adds about 27,600 gas per compliance action. Letting restrictive actions execute immediately while permissive and irreversible ones wait for a cancellable delay adds about 19,000 gas per immediate action. Sparse Merkle Tree commitments make list updates constant-cost but raise transfer cost by up to 2× and break the standard ERC-20 interface.

detail.abstract: The exponential rise of electronic waste (e-waste) threatens ecosystems, public health and carbon abatement efforts. As a major global generator, India transitioned from fragmented municipal handling to a structured statutory regime under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, establishing a digital Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) portal via the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. Institutional enforcement gaps and reliance on unorganized recycling impede progress on SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 16 (Strong Institutions). This study examines the legal intersection of climate action and institutional accountability. The primary objectives are to: (1) evaluate the legal efficacy and implementation hurdles of India's 2022 EPR framework; (2) analyse the regulatory role of environmental authorities (CPCB/SPCBs) and judicial mandates under SDG 16 and (3) formulate legal pathways harmonizing sustainable e-waste management with national climate targets under SDG 13. Employing doctrinal and normative legal research, this paper analyses statutory notifications, CPCB directives and landmark Supreme Court and National Green Tribunal jurisprudence under Article 21. An interdisciplinary policy framework assesses how digital EPR compliance systems impact carbon mitigation and toxic waste reduction. While the digital EPR portal has improved registration and tracking severe institutional deficits persist. The majority of e-waste remains in informal networks employing high-emission processing methods, undermining climate abatement. EPR certificate trading discrepancies, delayed verification and inadequate integration of informal workers impair regulatory transparency under SDG 16. Bridging SDG 13 and SDG 16 requires an integrated legal framework linking resource circularity with institutional integrity. Strengthening statutory oversight, enforcing strict noncompliance liability and formalizing informal waste collectors serve as legal pathways for India and developing nations to achieve sustainable environmental governance.

detail.abstract: Banks' holdings of municipal bonds can induce regulatory forbearance. We establish this fact using U.S. bank balance sheets and enforcement actions over 2002-2019. Our identification strategy instruments banks' holdings with the tax advantages that states offer for investing in municipal bonds. Consistent with public authorities' interest in protecting local government financing, forbearance is stronger among low-capital banks and where weak competitors, illiquid municipal bonds, or greater local government financing needs make bank support more valuable. This effect is stronger among politically connected banks, suggesting that political access helps translate these financing concerns into regulatory accommodation.

detail.abstract:
Background: Hosting the FIFA World Cup is frequently associated with expectations of economic growth, infrastructure development, international visibility, and lasting social benefits. However, the extent to which these anticipated legacies materialise remains contested. While mega-sporting events can create opportunities for long-term development, their outcomes vary considerably across host countries and institutional contexts.

Objective: This study examines the economic and societal legacies of FIFA World Cups, focusing on the contextual and governance-related factors that influence whether hosting produces sustainable benefits beyond the event itself.

Methods: The study employs a qualitative research approach, combining frame analysis and qualitative content analysis of relevant literature and evidence on FIFA World Cup legacies. Descriptive quantitative summaries complement the qualitative analysis to identify recurring patterns and relationships between legacy outcomes and their underlying conditions.

Results: The analysis highlights the importance of long-term strategic planning, institutional capacity, stakeholder coordination, and post-event utilisation in shaping legacy outcomes. Economic and societal benefits cannot be assumed to follow automatically from hosting a FIFA World Cup. Instead, their realisation depends on how effectively event-related investments, infrastructure, and development initiatives are integrated into broader national and local strategies.

Conclusion: FIFA World Cup legacies should be understood not as inevitable consequences of hosting, but as context-dependent outcomes shaped by governance structures, institutional capabilities, and strategic decisions. The study contributes to a more differentiated understanding of mega-event legacies and emphasises the importance of evaluating long-term benefits in relation to the conditions under which they emerge.

detail.abstract: We examine whether campaign contributions enable U.S. health insurers to obtain firmspecific rents. Using insurer-state-year data and a difference-indifferences design, we exploit two legal shocks: state pay-to-play laws that tighten constraints on political exchange and McDonnell v. United States that weakened federal anti-corruption enforcement. We estimate that pay-to-play laws reduce insurers' contributions to political candidates by 28.1% and reduce contributing insurers' Medicare premium revenue by 49.5%. Pay-to-play laws are also associated with more active supervisory intervention, lower Medicaid spending per enrollee, and better household insurance affordability. Insurers with greater premium exposure to adopting states experience lower profitability. By contrast, following McDonnell v. United States, insurer contributions and public-program premiums increase more in highthan in low-corruption states. Overall, our findings suggest that pay-to-play laws can curb insurer rents from preferential public-program allocation and supervisory forbearance, with implications for public spending and health care affordability.

detail.abstract: This study examined how closely self-reported generative AI (GenAI) literacy corresponds to tested knowledge, focusing on item content and respondents’ current use of GenAI. Using an online survey of 5,000 adults aged 20–69 in Japan, we compared a 14-item self-report scale with a ten-item scored test. Correlations with the test varied widely with item content, from .370 for understanding of mechanisms and risks to .084 for basic use, and the total score fell between them at .225. Among the 2,626 respondents who did not currently use GenAI, the corresponding correlations were .265 and −.127. Associations with technology acceptance constructs also differed depending on whether literacy was measured by the test or by self-report, and on model specification. The findings indicate that a total self-report score should not be treated as a proxy for tested knowledge without considering item content, the coverage of the criterion test and respondents’ use status.

title: Microstructure Invariance and Algorithmic Order Flow: Intraday VWAP Work Efficiency and Dark Pool Decomposition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract:
Modern equity market microstructure has undergone a profound structural transformation: over 45% to 60% of institutional transaction volume is now routed away from continuous lit limit order books into off-exchange Alternative Trading Systems (ATS), wholesale internalizers, algorithmic parent-to-child execution slices (TWAP, VWAP, POV), and Market-on-Close (MOC) auction crosses. Consequently, classical order-flow metrics relying on displayed quotes or naive open-to-close bar polarity suffer from severe attenuation bias and directional misclassification during high-absorption consolidation regimes (e.g., Dragonfly and Gravestone Doji formations).

Grounded in Kyle and Obizhaeva's (2016) Microstructure Invariance hypothesis and the First-Principles Market Mechanics (FPMM) framework, this paper establishes an orthogonal decomposition architecture for visible and covert institutional order flows. First, we decompose the square-root price impact functional into transient order-book viscosity and permanent barycentric displacement relative to the session Volume-Weighted Average Price (P_VWAP), deriving the dimensionless Barycentric Mechanical Efficiency operator (VWAP_PDE) under regularized lower-quartile turnover damping (gamma_min). Second, we formulate a Close Location Value (CLV) Hybrid Momentum Kernel (Delta M_k) that couples inter-bar gap memory with intra-bar shadow geometry, formally proving its exact sign recovery under zero-body Doji sweeps. Third, by isolating off-exchange FINRA Trade Reporting Facility (TRF) disclosures, high-kurtosis algorithmic block bursts, and tail-end MOC auction imbalances, we construct a bounded, singularity-free Positive-Part Dark Energy Ratio (Dark_Ratio in [0, 100%]).

Empirical evaluations across 171,200 point-in-time S&P 100 stock-day observations (2020-2026) demonstrate that our orthogonal dark-flow decomposition substantially outperforms classical microstructure benchmarks---including Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading (VPIN), Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov Order Flow Imbalance (OFI), and Chaikin Money Flow (CMF). Executing strictly at next-session opening auction prints (t+1) under a state-hysteresis holding protocol (26.8-day mean holding horizon; 9.4x annualized turnover) net of transaction costs, the FPMM Dark-Efficiency Composite strategy achieves an out-of-sample net Sharpe ratio of 1.08 (NW t-stat = 2.92, maximum drawdown -15.6%) and retains an annualized seven-factor net alpha of +5.8% (t-stat = 2.92).

detail.abstract:
Classical formal logic has suffered a complete institutional collapse, fragmented into computer science protocols, abstract mathematics, and scholastic philosophical commentary. This institutional removal has left human cognitive systems unprotected against epistemological noise, algorithmic manipulation, and manufactured consensus. This paper introduces Cognistics—an original universal discipline and conceptual framework established by the author to supersede Aristotelian canons.

Designed as an enduring cognitive architecture for civilizational intelligence, Cognistics transforms static logical laws into dynamic, substrate-independent operational principles: Contextual Superposition, Cognitive Invariance, Dialectical Dynamics, Epistemic Grounding, and Chrono-Resilience. By unifying multi-agent synthetic networks, quantum processing, and biological cognition, Cognistics provides a structural foundation for long-range intellectual sovereignty.

detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for foreign exchange (Forex) trading requires realistic execution modeling, interpretable reward design, and action spaces that respect market constraints. Existing approaches often simplify these aspects, limiting policy transparency and practical relevance. This paper presents a modular RL framework integrating three components: (1) a friction-aware execution engine enforcing anti-lookahead semantics-observations at close 𝑡 , execution at open 𝑡+1 , and markto-market at close 𝑡+1-while modeling spread, commission, slippage, rollover financing, and margintriggered liquidation; (2) a decomposable 11-component reward architecture with fixed, pre-specified weights and per-step logging, enabling attribution, ablation, and auditability; and (3) a 10-action discrete interface supporting scaling, reduction, closure, and reversal, with legal-action masking enforcing margin-aware feasibility during training and evaluation. Empirical evaluation on EURUSD training-split data reveals non-monotonic interactions among reward components, demonstrating that additional penalties do not consistently improve performance. The full reward configuration achieves a terminal training Sharpe ratio of 0.765 and cumulative return of 57.09%. Comparing action spaces, the extended 10-action interface increases cumulative return but reduces Sharpe relative to a conservative 3-action variant, revealing a return-activity trade-off under a fixed training budget. Scaling-enabled strategies consistently reduce drawdowns, with the combined configuration delivering the strongest endpoint performance. Supplementary diagnostics on GBPUSD, USDJPY, and AUDUSD exhibit qualitatively similar trends. These findings demonstrate the framework's diagnostic value and underscore the importance of controlled, interpretable design in RL-based financial systems.

detail.abstract: Contemporary sustainability research remains heavily constrained by a reliance on technological interventions to mitigate ecological decay. This commentary critiques this paradigm by demonstrating how technical efficiency often acts as an accelerator of resource extraction rather than a solution to material dependency. By integrating behavioral metrics into traditional ecological-impact models, this article shifts the analytical lens from external engineering fixes to internal structural transformation. We utilize a radical political economy framework to trace how the structural legacy of neoliberal Structural Adjustment Programmes (SAPs) has marketised public architecture, engineering a matrix of elite capture and acute institutional insolvency. This systemic crisis is exposed through the 2026 Kenyan public university financial collapse and the historic 28-day countrywide solidarity strike executed across all cadres by UASU, KUSU, and KUDHEIHA. Crucially, we demonstrate that this mobilization was not a narrow dispute over academic salaries, but an organic, multi-cadre class rejection of the peripheral capitalist state, uniting academic faculty with agricultural, support, and non-teaching workers. We model collective psychological wellbeing as a non-linear inverse function of the wealth distribution gap (the Gini index). This demonstrates that systemic inequality drives destabilising, high-emission conspicuous consumption as a defense mechanism against relative deprivation. Finally, drawing on the re-formulated Coupled Climate-Economy-Biosphere (CoCEB) framework, we propose that Universal Basic Income (UBI) serves as a critical macroeconomic vehicle for Samir Amin's doctrine of "delinking." By funding UBI through a designated fraction of the global warming abatement share, the state contractually decompresses inequality, bypasses centralized nodes prone to elite capture, and prevents post-colonial resources from being siphoned into top-heavy carbon monopolies managed by Western metropolitan NGOs, providing a formula-driven path toward securing our shared progress.

detail.abstract: Forecast comparisons inform investment and other economic decisions, but machine learning forecasts can be trained under objectives that differ from the relevant losses. Estimation error can then create spurious evidence of predictive superiority, even with out-of-sample evaluation. We establish feasible inference for differences in population evaluation risks in this setting. Building on locally robust estimation, we construct scores that preserve the risk target and remove first-order estimation sensitivity. Under geometric beta-mixing, moment conditions and simultaneous learning bounds, we establish Gaussian limits and consistent long-run covariance estimation for overlapping chronological training windows, allowing refitting at every evaluation date. Uniform extensions provide confidence coverage over classes of data-generating processes; Wald inference requires nondegenerate corrected-score covariance. For sparse linear forecasts and neural probability forecasts, we give explicit corrections and simultaneous learning bounds. Simulations with lasso and neural forecasts show substantial reductions in size distortion that bootstrapping uncorrected scores does not reproduce.

detail.abstract: Embodied Biographical Alignment (EBA) considers the possibility that some alignment-relevant capabilities may depend not only on information about human experience, but also on causally structured developmental history. This version refines the experimental core of EBA after a series of toy pilots in which history-generated differences could, in many cases, be reproduced through replay, terminal-state transfer, or reconstruction of update dynamics. These negative and constraining results motivate a stricter formulation: the lived agent must be preserved as an independent developmental reference, while synthetic baselines should be compared with it not only on current behavior but also on subsequent learning under genuinely novel demands. The design introduces a patient-zero protocol, a partial clone with developmental amnesia, the working concept of Latent Developmental Reserve, and Source-level population transfer. The central problem is developmental equivalence: which consequences of a causally lived history must be preserved for a reconstructed agent-and subsequently the Source-to remain the same future learner when the future relevance of particular fragments of history is not known in advance. The paper does not claim the existence of machine emotions, qualia, or intrinsically non-copyable experience; it specifies an experiment whose design does not rule out such a functional residue in advance.

detail.abstract: Papers on large-language-model (LLM) trading agents and alpha mining report Sharpe ratios that would be remarkable in any other part of empirical finance. We audit the evidence behind those numbers. Before coding a single paper we pre-registered a population of 91 papers from a curated corpus of LLM trading research, a ten-field coding rubric, an analysis script and five directional hypotheses, and committed all of them to version control. Every code is backed by a verbatim quote that a script checks against the paper's text, and a second, blind coder recoded a random 20%. Of the 75 papers with a trading test, 51% deduct no trading costs and only 9% model costs from data; the median test window is 12 months, and a quarter of windows are six months or shorter. Among the 51 papers whose test window is not known to lie after the model's training cutoff, 98% neither test after the cutoff, nor evaluate live, nor use a chronologically consistent model. Only 9% report a multiplicity-adjusted result, and just five papers combine deducted costs, a leakage control and a reported trial count. Two of the five hypotheses pass (short windows; uncontrolled look-ahead). Three fail: more papers report a trial count than we predicted, though most of those counts are repeated random seeds rather than the number of strategies searched; and the predicted links between headline Sharpe and test-window length, and between headline Sharpe and costs, are not detectable in the 13 papers that state a headline Sharpe in their abstract or conclusion. We release the codes, quotes and script, and propose a six-line reporting minimum.

detail.abstract: This article examines whether New Zealand's legal framework is equipped to address the rise of nonconsensual sexualised deepfakes generated generative AI tools integrated into social media platforms. While platforms such as X and Meta increasingly deploy AI systems capable of producing realistic synthetic images, these technologies have intensified gendered abuse, disproportionately targeting women. Using a Grok-generated deepfake incident as a case study, the article evaluates the applicability and limitations of the Harmful Digital Communications Act 2015, privacy torts, defamation, and negligence. Although the proposed Deepfake Digital Harm and Exploitation Bill may close definitional gaps, criminalisation alone cannot address systemic risks created by platform design, business incentives, and inadequate safeguards.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the relationship between equity markets and exchange rates using a multivariate Granger model against the S&P 500. We compare the multivariate VAR model against independent Granger causality tests to establish significance. A relationship between stock markets and exchange rates would hold value concerning the implications of fiscal and monetary policy, investor strategy, and crisis prediction. We analyze the S&P 500's predictive relationship with exchange rates in conjunction with STOXX 600 (USD/EUR), ASX 200 (USD/AUD), Straits Time Index (USD/SGD), Nikkei 225 (USD/JPY), Swiss Market Index (USD/CHF) and FTSE 100 (USD/GBP). We follow through with analyzing how altering the granularity affects these results. We find evidence in support of the flow and portfolio balance models, concluding that daily data provides a stronger signal than monthly data, which has no Granger causality for the flow model and some Granger causality for the portfolio balance model. We also find evidence of multivariate VAR demonstrating Granger causality for scenarios where corresponding independent tests fail.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the production of legal doctrine during the transition from individualized to general corporate law in the nineteenth-century United States. Beginning in the 1840s, states prohibited the issuance of special corporate charters, replacing firm-specific legislative privileges with general laws to access the corporate form. To measure the effect of these reforms on doctrinal output, I apply text-as-data methods to historical published state case law. Using a staggered difference-indifferences design, I find that the doctrinal content of published judicial opinions more than doubled following the prohibition of special corporate charters. The effect is concentrated not only in corporate doctrine, but in the property and contract domains as well. Further, I demonstrate that doctrine increased in two areas commonly outlined in special charters: i) public land rights and infrastructure and ii) debt contracts. I interpret these results as evidence of institutional substitution, where the charter bans put the onus on courts to produce new general law to replace the individualized law that characterized special charters.

title: The Zero-Days-to-Expiry Put-Credit Premium from Traded Option Bars: Real, Mostly Not Drift, and Priced by First-Day Shocks

detail.title: The Zero-Days-to-Expiry Put-Credit Premium from Traded Option Bars: Real, Mostly Not Drift, and Priced by First-Day Shocks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author develops and maintains the open-source research engine described in this paper. No external party funded, reviewed or influenced this work.
declarations.funderStatement: None. This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Selling a short-dated put credit spread on a large-cap index fund collects a premium almost every day and gives much of it back on a few days. We ask whether that premium exists once it is priced from actual traded option bars rather than modeled marks, whether it is anything more than the market's upward drift, and whether any rule stated in advance can avoid its losses. The structure is a zero-days-to-expiry (0DTE) SPY put credit spread, entered in the morning and held to mechanical settlement, on roughly two and a half years of OPRA option bars. Every test is a frozen contract run through Autonomous Quant Researcher, an open-source engine with chronological splits, a one-use holdout, a weekly-cluster bootstrap and a drift-neutral residual control. The base cell earns +55.7 and +71.6 basis points of width per session after an assumed round-trip cost of 0.5% of width in discovery and validation, with a gross win rate of 95.2%. Market direction explains 13-30% of the gross payoff, and the residual is positive in both splits. The premium is monotone in moneyness and replicates in shape on QQQ. It does not clear the pre-registered bar: on both tapes the discovery weekly bootstrap lower bound sits just below zero. A calm-day filter makes every bound worse, because the losses come on the first day of a shock, which follows a calm day. Of 120 pre-registered intraday management rules, none beats holding. A language-model rule that passed discovery and validation with net Sharpe ratios of 2.94 and 3.34 fell to 0.26 on its single holdout use. The premium is real, mostly not drift, and paid for by shocks that prior-day information does not forecast. The bar was not moved.

title: Testing the Premises Behind Popular Technical-Analysis Scripts under Pre-Registration
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Testing the Premises Behind Popular Technical-Analysis Scripts under Pre-Registration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author develops and maintains the open-source research engine described in this paper. No external party funded, reviewed or influenced this work.
declarations.funderStatement: None. This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The most popular technical-analysis scripts on retail charting platforms are not textbook indicators but drawn constructs: Fibonacci retracements, regression channels, moving-average ribbons, recency-weighted support levels and pivot-anchored channels. Testing each script would test its author. We instead extract the small number of falsifiable premises the scripts share and test each one, at its conventional parameters, with one frozen rule and no parameter search. We add eight textbook oscillator claims, the volatility-squeeze premise, five pivot-anchored channel claims at a published script's defaults, a 232-cell grid of single-condition daily rules, and a hidden-Markov-model (HMM) regime trading system. Every test was pre-registered, run through one open-source engine with a fixed battery of nine gates, judged on a session-weighted portfolio mean, and compared with simply being long. Nothing is supported. One premise, a rising regression channel bought at its lower band, passed all nine discovery gates and then lost 22 bps per session in validation. In validation every drawn-construct premise did worse than being long, the 0.618 Fibonacci decile was beaten by both of its neighbours in both windows, the squeeze preceded moves half the size of an ordinary session, and channel breakouts reverted on both sides at once. All four discovery passers in the rule grid were one feature in both directions, an artifact of a window in which being invested paid. We report every rule, and we explain why several holdouts were deliberately left unread.

detail.abstract: This study proposes the Carbon Adjusted Standardized Sharpe Ratio (CASSR), which combines standardized Sharpe ratios and portfolio carbon exposure using parameters estimated from the feasible portfolio distribution. For Bitcoin, gold, and the S&P 500, CASSR reduces calculated carbon exposure by 33.28% relative to Sharpe optimization, with a 3.51% reduction in the Sharpe ratio. The optimal allocation remains unchanged under the alternative emission estimates examined but varies with gold valuation and investment horizon. In a separate application to eleven S&P 500 sectors using a common carbon metric, CASSR reduces carbon exposure by 93.20%, with a 13.56% reduction in the Sharpe ratio. Moving-block bootstrap results indicate lower average portfolio carbon exposure under CASSR. Comparisons with alternative carbonoptimization approaches place the CASSR solution on both the carbon-efficient and meanvariance-carbon efficient frontiers. The findings are conditional on the selected investment universe and carbon-accounting assumptions.

detail.abstract: Community Benefit Frameworks (CBFs), which are often referred to as Community Benefit Agreements (CBAs), have proliferated as local governments and communities have struggled to address the risks and benefits arising from the rapid growth of data centers. Our research identified 22 publicly available CBFs, and this Article uses summary statistics and specific examples to describe the key provisions of these agreements. The CBFs include a variety of agreement types from across the country entered into over a period of nearly seven years. The Article explores the ways that communities are securing legally binding benefits from data center developers through CBFs, and it identifies the common features of CBFs, the community and developer benefits of CBFs, and potential vulnerabilities. The Article concludes that the provisions included in CBFs for data centers vary widely on many of the most contested issues regarding data centers, and it suggests the need for further research to identify the effects of these agreements on communities and the AI sector and to identify the core features necessary to ensure that these agreements are welfare-enhancing.

detail.abstract: In empirical economics, regression discontinuity design (RDD) inference is commonly conducted using asymptotic normality under an independence assumption for simplicity, even though running variables or disturbances may exhibit complex dependence difficult to model. We first rigorously identify a fundamental dilemma for conventional asymptotic-normality-based RDD inference. To address this dilemma, we propose a validity recovery procedure that redefines the roles of bias and stochastic calibration, and thus decouples data dependence from stochastic calibration. Taking the independence-assumption-based confidence interval as our inferential anchor, our procedure restores its validity even when the original observations are dependent. More specifically, for fixed-design RDD inference based on local linear regression, compared with the conventional approach, in addition to asymptotically exact nominal coverage, our intervals exploit higher-order smoothness without enlarging the asymptotic variance constant, and attain the minimax-optimal shrinking rates up to a mild factor, such as √ log T. The leading constants of radii also asymptotically match those of independence-assumption-based intervals. This procedure requires neither specific dependence frameworks, such as mixing or physical dependence, nor dependence-modeling techniques, such as long-run variance estimation. For random-design RDD, under more specific dependence assumptions, we investigate the rate-explicit coverage error at each prescribed nominal level and characterize the trade-off between this rate and interval length. This procedure also offers substantial benefits for coverage: modeling dependence becomes an optional enhancement for inference that can further enable validity recovery and improve finite-sample coverage, while averaging over repeated calibrations stabilizes the randomized center and protects against undercoverage in finite samples without increasing interval length. In short, under mild dependence and moment conditions, our procedure makes data independence an implementation default for inference rather than a validity requirement. Simulations support the theoretical results.

title: The Code of Agentic Commerce

detail.abstract:
The coming era of commerce will be driven not by human consumers choosing among websites but by artificially intelligent software agents advising and increasingly purchasing on behalf of consumers. In this emerging world of agentic commerce, the most important decisions occur before the consumer ever sees a checkout page, such as how the AI agent ranks available options and what commissions retailers will pay it. How the transition to agentic commerce unfolds has large-scale implications for household affordability, the distribution of wealth, and the viability of small businesses.

Yet the governing rules of agentic commerce are being written by dispersed actors who do not necessarily see themselves as collectively designing market infrastructure.  Judges and regulators are extending consumer protection, antitrust, and common law written for simpler human relations to transactions intermediated by AI agents. At the same time, AI providers and online retailers are negotiating universal technical protocols and contractual arrangements that function as private law.

This Article offers an account of these developments as distributed rulemaking through public laws, private contracts, and technical protocols. It identifies important legal barriers that are making it less likely that agentic commerce fulfills its significant potential for societal gains. It also develops a legal framework for pushing AI agents to put consumers’ interests first, provide opportunities to small businesses, and maximize economic productivity. This is a constitutional moment for agentic commerce. Private decisions that look technical or transactional are poised to become commercial infrastructure that will be difficult to change later. The law can play a major role in building that infrastructure on trust and access rather than on opacity and gatekeeping.

title: Straight Borders are not a Curse

detail.abstract: The artificial-states literature associates straight borders with harmful political partition. We test this view within countries. We construct a GIS-based measure of border straightness for 1,639 subnational regions and relate it to regional GDP per capita over 1950-2020, comparing regions in the same country and year. Straightness is positively associated with income: a 10-percentage-point increase in a region's straight-border share is associated with about 4.8 percent higher GDP per capita. Domestic and international straightness both enter positively, and their coefficients are not statistically different. The association is positive in countries with low and medium ethnic fractionalization, and negative but imprecise in highly fractionalized ones. We interpret these patterns through the processes that create borders. Straight lines can reflect harmful partition, but also administrative organization and negotiated coordination. Border geometry alone is a poor proxy for harmful artificiality.

title: Agency Conflicts and Financial Covenants: Theory and Estimates of Control Rights
affiliations: HEC Paris

detail.title: Agency Conflicts and Financial Covenants: Theory and Estimates of Control Rights

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: This work has benefited from a State grant managed by the Agence Nationale de la Recherche under the Investissements d’Avenir programme with the reference ANR-18-EURE-0005 / EUR DATA EFM.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the relationship between financial covenant design, enforcement, and the impacts of violations, and how this relationship has evolved alongside the secular trends in violations and post-violation interventions. I develop an optimal contracting model in which covenants arise endogenously from a hidden effort problem and non-contractible interim action. By allocating contingent control rights, financial covenants mitigate the lack of cash-flow pledgeability and facilitate financing. I estimate the model using Simulated Method of Moments, targeting causally identified moments from the reduced-form covenant literature. The full-sample estimates reveal that violation rates are primarily governed by the hidden effort problem and performance signal structure, while intervention rates are largely driven by the costs and benefits of interim action. Subperiod estimates show that the weakening impact of covenant violations on managerial discipline is reflected in higher intervention rates, but not in the secular decline in violation rates. The rise of PE sponsorship explains around one quarter of the estimated structural shift.

title: Corporate Culture Choices in Bertrand Competition: Customer Orientation versus Corporate Social Responsibility
affiliations: Institute for Economic Sciences

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.

detail.abstract: This paper examines firms' endogenous choice between customer orientation (CO) and corporate social responsibility (CSR) in a Bertrand duopoly with differentiated products. In the first stage, each firm simultaneously and independently selects the optimal level of its corporate culture, specifically regarding CO and CSR; in the second stage, each firm simultaneously and independently sets its price to maximize its objective function. Using subgame-perfect equilibrium, we compare profits under CO, which values the surplus of a firm's own customers, and CSR, which values aggregate consumer surplus. We show that firms earn the same equilibrium profits for all feasible corporate culture levels. This result differs sharply from the corresponding Cournot result, in which firms prefer CO, and highlights how the mode of competition shapes corporate culture choices.

detail.abstract: We exploit plausibly exogenous variation in court-president appointments in Italy and show that leadership turnover slows the growth in the duration of bankruptcy proceedings. These effects are larger when incoming presidents are younger, have prior managerial experience, or are locally rooted in the court’s jurisdiction, suggesting that career concerns and organizational learning play an important part. Improved judicial efficiency strengthens creditor rights through the credit channel: bank lending expands, late payments decline, and larger firms reallocate investment towards intangible assets.

No human participants were recruited, interviewed or observed, and no identifiable personal data were collected. Institutional ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was independently developed and conducted by the author.

detail.abstract: Self-help housing can increase residents' influence over their homes while transferring construction work, financial exposure and management burdens to households unable to absorb them. This paper asks how architectural support and public schemes can protect participation and deliver an adequate first dwelling without depending on later expansion. A critical integrative review of Indian policy, housing theory and six precedents is combined with descriptive secondary analysis. In the Uttar Pradesh audit sample, 1,129 of 2,079 houses recorded complete lacked dedicated cooking space. Public rural temperature measurements further illustrate why material classification and recorded completion cannot describe occupied performance. Sonurli and Ekalara in Maharashtra are selected for an architectural application because historical housing and environmental data are available. A hypothetical household brief is tested through coordinated plans, a section, a construction and occupation sequence, a constrained 30 m² alternative and a historical rate-based estimate. The proposal separates resident decision authority from construction management and physical labour, which may be delegated to paid support. It requires an explicit response to interrupted work, insufficient funds and the absence of safe interim accommodation. PMAY-G already supplies part of this institutional basis; additional support requires lawful authority and appropriated resources. The tested brief exceeds identified construction assistance before unresolved costs are added. The contribution is an operational architectural synthesis with explicit funding and delivery failures, not demonstrated affordability or resident acceptance. Field verification, local quotations and an independently evaluated pilot are required before implementation. Generative AI disclosure: Generative AI tools assisted with drafting, editorial revision and manuscript preparation. Responsibility for the evidence, calculations, interpretation and the submitted version rests with the named author.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between food palatability, portion adequacy, and student satisfaction with hostel food services at the Army Institute of Business Administration (Army IBA), Sylhet, Bangladesh. It focuses on two key dimensions of food service quality: food palatability, including taste, aroma, appearance, texture, and menu variety, and portion adequacy, referring to the sufficiency and consistency of food servings. Drawing on existing literature on institutional dining and student food satisfaction, the study highlights the importance of these factors in residential educational settings, where students largely depend on institution-provided meals. A structured questionnaire comprising demographic, Likert-scale, and open-ended questions is included to examine students' experiences and perceptions. The study aims to provide insights that may support improvements in hostel food services, student well-being, and institutional dining management.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) capital is concentrated among larger firms, yet its positive association with organic investment is stronger among smaller firms. Using a firm-year measure of accumulated AI capital constructed from AI-skilled employment, market valuations, and a capital-accumulation framework, we examine organic investment among U.S. publicly traded firms. A one-standard-deviation increase in lagged AI capital is associated with 22.10% higher subsequent organic investment, measured by capital expenditures and R&D net of proceeds from asset sales. Instrumental variable estimates based on predetermined exposure to AI-intensive universities support the baseline finding. Despite larger firms' greater accumulation of AI capital, the estimated investment relation declines with firm size. Additional evidence links AI capital to greater stock-market liquidity, lower financing costs, and higher operating efficiency. These findings highlight a distinction between where technological capital accumulates and where it is most strongly associated with internal investment.

detail.abstract:
In 2005 Ametex was Bolivia's largest textile exporter, sewing garments for U.S. brands and employing more than 4,000 workers in El Alto. Its business depended on a temporary U.S. trade preference (ATPA/ATPDEA), it never covered its interest expense even in its best years, and it was financed with bank debt and bonds bought by Bolivian pension funds. When the preferences were suspended in 2008 the company collapsed; its bonds defaulted, pension funds wrote off more than USD 18.5 million, and in 2012 the state created Enatex to keep the plant running, until it was closed in 2016 after a deficit of Bs 388 million. Using 2003-2012 financial statements, the case asks why the owners did not sell or liquidate during the 2003-2005 exit window, and how a change in labor rules (Supreme Decree 28699) destroyed the abandonment option. Topics: liquidation value, real options, early-warning ratios, creditor behavior, sunk-cost bias and state-owned enterprises.

Resumen en español: caso de enseñanza sobre Ametex, la mayor exportadora textil de Bolivia, su dependencia del ATPDEA, el default de sus bonos en manos de las AFP y su paso a la empresa estatal Enatex. ¿Por qué no salieron a tiempo? Versión original en español disponible a solicitud del autor.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the data revolution promotes firms' organic investment at the firm level. Using newly developed firm-level measures of data assets, we document that data-rich firms undertake significantly more capital and R&D investment. Although data assets are concentrated among large firms, their relation with organic investment is substantially stronger among smaller firms. The organic interpretation of these investments is supported by evidence that data assets enhance investment efficiency, primarily by mitigating underinvestment. Consistent with an information-and-financing channel, greater data assets are also associated with better information environments, greater stock-market liquidity, and a lower cost of equity. The operating results also provide a useful contrast with prior evidence on AI and product innovation: greater data assets are associated with higher operating efficiency, lower operating costs, and higher productivity. The results are robust to alternative proxies for data assets and to instrumental-variable specifications. Overall, the evidence suggests that data assets are associated with stronger organic growth among smaller firms, despite being more heavily concentrated among large firms.

detail.abstract: This note compares what S&P 500 companies say about acquisition-related cyber risk in their latest 10-K risk factors (Item 1A) with the processes they describe in the cybersecurity disclosure required since 2023 (Item 1C). Of 482 companies with a usable Item 1A, 96 (19.9%) state that acquisitions expose them to cyber or data risk. Of 465 with a usable Item 1C, 21 (4.5%) describe a process for acquisition targets or acquired businesses. Among the 459 companies with both items, 87 of the 96 that state the risk (90.6%) describe no such process, although companies that state the risk are about three times as likely to describe one as those that do not (9.4% against 3.3%), also after controls for size, sector and acquisition activity. Of the 16 process disclosures that address the period after closing, five tie a named team or role to the work and seven state an end point or integration end state; only one does both, none pairs an owner with a condition for ending the interim period, and none states a numeric deadline. The same holds in each company's two preceding filings. AI models coded the filings with blind second coding, an independent reader re-coded the owner and end-point attributes, and the author resolved disagreements. The findings describe disclosure, not practice. The note closes with implications for investors and boards.

detail.abstract: Studies of connectivity and accessibility measure the opportunities transport networks make available to individuals but rarely analyse the frequency and reliability of those connections. Combining a range of newly available official open datasets on rail provision and operational performance across Great Britain, I geocode, quality control and harmonise a range of variables that are of interest for both research and policy. The key variables include frequency, cancellation and delay rates, and frequency-adjusted disruption indices. The dataset and accompanying code cover 309 million scheduled station calls between 2,599 stations across 45 four-weekly periods between April 2023 and September 2026. Given the point-level nature of the data, I then provide statistics at station, local authority district and International Territorial Level 3, 2 and 1 regional scales as well as Travel to Work Areas-allowing flexible understanding of the spatial clustering of (un)reliability of rail provision. As the frequency of data releases increases, our methods to analyse this data transparently must also improve, and so the lightweight pipeline enables easy updating from subsequent four-weekly releases. Copying and pasting four lines of code runs this station-geocodinganalysis pipeline end-to-end, downloading the most up-to-date data, cleaning and providing descriptive summaries. On most computers this will take around five minutes to reproduce and/or update. For policymakers, the online visualiser † provides an up-to-date foundation for investigating geographical inequalities in dependable transport connectivity and their relationship with wider urban and regional conditions.

title: Agency Guidance After Slaughter: Administering Law Without Making It
affiliations: 2. Independent Researcher and Consultant

detail.title: Agency Guidance After Slaughter: Administering Law Without Making It

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I was previously Policy Director of the Antitrust Division and co-authored the 2023 Merger Guidelines.
declarations.funderStatement: No funder.

detail.abstract:
Agency guidance is not law; guidance merely supports the administration of law. That's a good thing--Justice Gorsuch reminded us in his Trump v. Slaughter concurrence that the founders rightfully feared when "the legislative and executive powers are united in the same person."  The majority opinion in Slaughter, of course, washed away an already-contestable foundation of the alternative view that antitrust guidance might desirably make or change the law. Federal Trade Commissioners can no longer be imagined to be neutral technocrats; for better or worse, they are now unquestionably the servants of the President. And the President cannot make law absent express delegation from Congress. 

Slaughter caps a decade of administrative law changes that will impact not only formal rulemaking, but non-binding policy statements such as the antitrust guidance documents issued by the President's officials at the Federal Trade Commission and the DOJ's Antitrust Division. The lesson for guidance used to provide predictability in the absence of delegated rulemaking authority is clear: guidance can and should transparently describe how agencies apply the law but must not create it. 

This Essay explains how these developments, and the changes to historical guidance practice that have followed, will support the growing project to steer antitrust toward being a regime of law. Diverse authors have recognized that antitrust for too long drifted from law, and a burgeoning subfield of scholarship has begun to ground antitrust policy on legal foundations, moving beyond purposive debates to a discussion consistent with the modern Supreme Court's interpretive approach to the rest of the cathedral.  That is where antitrust should go. This Essay explains how guidance documents can further this trend (and can avoid undermining it).

detail.abstract:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a common inherited cardiac disorder whose variable presentation can complicate timely diagnosis. This study evaluated deep-learning approaches for classifying HCM from cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images. A publicly available dataset containing 59,267 CMR images from healthy individuals and patients with HCM was reorganized and supplemented with 2,000 class-balanced synthetic images generated using a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN). The resulting dataset was split into training, validation, and test subsets and used to compare a custom convolutional neural network (CNN), ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18, and ResNet-50 models. Automatic mixed-precision training on an A100 GPU was used to improve computational efficiency.

Among the evaluated models, DCGAN-augmented ResNet-18 produced the strongest reported test performance, achieving 99.63% accuracy with a loss of 0.0107, compared with 98.65% accuracy for ResNet-50 and 95.63% for the custom CNN. Mixed-precision optimization reduced training time and memory consumption while improving baseline model performance. These findings suggest that a comparatively shallow residual network can effectively classify HCM-related CMR image patterns when combined with transfer learning and synthetic augmentation. However, the reported results are limited to the study dataset and image-level evaluation; patient-level evaluation, independent multicenter validation, bias assessment, and explainability analysis are necessary before clinical use.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence promises a legal system that is cheap, fast, and always within reach. In Superjustice, Samuel Becher and Benjamin Alarie make that promise more fully than any book I know, and on access to justice they are right. This review asks what the promise costs. Much of social life runs on informal norms, relationships, forbearance, and equitable judgment rather than on law, and some of that order depends on the very costs and gaps in formal law that the book wants to remove. Drawing on behavioral law and economics and the law-and-norms literature, the review argues that a legal system that sees nearly everything may bring more AI and more law, but fewer norms. Removing legal friction can crowd out the cheaper, relationship-preserving ways in which people settle disputes. AI is likely to see formal, data-dense wrongs much more easily than contested ones, pulling conduct toward law and spreading scrutiny unevenly. And systems that detect and judge misconduct on our behalf may weaken the moral judgment and informal sanctioning on which norms depend. The review closes with a deployment test that assigns AI one of four roles, as enforcer, witness, facilitator, or corrective. The goal is a legal system that grows better without simply growing bigger.

detail.abstract: Missed radiographic abnormalities in the emergency department have a well-documented error rate of 11 to 20% in high-volume trauma centers, with significant implications for patient outcome and clinical liability. Current deep learning systems solve the problem as single-view binary classification, neglecting the multi-view synthesis that radiologists conduct as part of their usual workflow and failing to give spatial or morphological justification for their decisions. In this paper, we propose an explainable multi-task deep learning framework called X-BONE that addresses two critical gaps in existing fracture detection systems: susceptibility to bias from single-view analysis and a lack of clinical interpretability. X-BONE leverages a hierarchical Swin Transformer backbone with a proposed Cross-View Attention (CVA) mechanism to combine diagnostic information across multiple views of the same lesion, utilizes multi-task prediction heads for joint classification, localization, and fracture typing, and offers Score-CAM explainability for gradient-free spatial reasoning. Trained on 40,561 images from 14,863 MURA studies and evaluated on 1,199 patient-level validation studies across seven anatomical regions, X-BONE achieves an AUC of 0.8953, F1 of 78.78%, and a Disparate Impact Ratio of 0.910, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance with equitable cross-anatomy generalization. Cross-View Attention contributes the single largest performance gain (+37.5 AUC points over max pooling), and the ablation experiments support the value of multi-view reasoning for study-level diagnosis. Source code and trained weights are available upon request to support reproducibility.

detail.abstract: We study the optimal decumulation of retirement wealth under longevity and market risk. In particular, we focus on the transition between drawdown, which preserves liquidity and bequest potential, and annuitization, which provides a guaranteed lifetime income. We develop a flex-to-fix framework in which retirees remain invested and liquid before converting part or all of their wealth into an annuity at a later date. The flex-to-fix strategy has two limiting cases: immediate annuitization (fix-now) and permanent drawdown (fix-never). A static actuarial analysis shows that the optimal fixed conversion date depends strongly on the bequest motive, the withdrawal rate, and the return of the drawdown portfolio. There is no single optimal annuitization age across retirees, although optimal dates tend to concentrate around age 65 (retirement) or ages 75-80. Then, we develop two dynamic formulations that allow the conversion decision to respond to the retiree's realized wealth-income state. An optimal-stopping formulation shows that a well-chosen fixed date already captures most of the value of delaying annuitization, while state-contingent timing adds only a small further gain. A Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman variational inequality (HJBVI) formulation characterizes the free boundary governing a gradual transition from drawdown to annuity income. It also reveals an implicit bond effect of annuities on optimal equity allocation, and shows that spreading purchases over time substantially reduces market timing and ruin risk compared to single-date conversion rules. Finally, we propose approximating the HJBVI strategy with a simpler rule that spreads annuity purchases evenly across the flex window, once the optimal target date has been calibrated.
