detail.abstract: Online crowdsourcing contests generate rich dynamic behavior, but their core strategic state is latent: contestants react to noisy public leaderboard feedback rather than true relative performance. We develop a tractable dynamic game with Bayesian filtering and a corresponding structural estimation framework to recover effort costs, innovation risk, and feedback precision. With symmetric effort costs, sufficiently low innovation risk and effort costs, and the stated conditions on initial uncertainty and organizer preferences, a finite-precision design strictly outperforms every full-disclosure design, even when prizes and deadlines are reoptimized and precision has no direct cost. A closed-form leading-order effort policy links feedback precision to the range of perceived performance gaps over which prize incentives sustain effort, enabling tractable Bayesian estimation. For validation, we use a path-wise holdout design: private-leaderboard path values are excluded from the estimation likelihood and subsequently used for diagnostic tests, although ex post private-score information is used to define the focal rivalry. Across 73 Kaggle contests, higher estimated innovation risk is associated with greater private-path volatility, while higher estimated feedback precision is associated with smaller public-private gaps. These relationships also appear in time-split diagnostics and are interpreted as descriptive associations conditional on ex post focal-pair selection. Persistent differences across contests in score scale, evaluation metric, or submission frequency remain possible common drivers.

detail.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk assessment in resource-limited settings requires methods that capture complex interactions among risk factors beyond what conventional rulebased tools allow. This study proposes a clinical intelligence framework combining machine learning with medical domain expertise for multi-class CVD risk stratification. The framework reconstructs risk labels from a composite score computed over clinical variables, structured to mirror established cardiovascular risk models, and reports this relabeling transparently alongside the dataset's own original risk labels rather than treating either as ground truth. Feature engineering produces composite biomarkers including hemodynamic markers (pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure) and lipid ratios (TC/HDL, LDL/HDL). Strong regularization, stratified cross-validation, and Bayesian hyperparameter optimization guard against overfitting and label leakage. The framework compares regularized logistic regression against gradient boosting ensembles (CatBoost, XGBoost, Light-GBM) and their voting/stacking combinations on a Bangladeshi dataset (n=1,529), achieving 91.92% balanced accuracy and ROC-AUC of 0.984. Paired statistical testing (McNemar's exact test, bootstrap confidence intervals, Bonferroni correction) shows logistic regression significantly outperforms CatBoost and Light-GBM, while differences relative to XGBoost, voting, and stacking ensembles are not statistically significant. This approach supports early cardiovascular risk stratification in resource-constrained primary care settings using standard clinical measurements.

title: Sixty Nights of Overnight Trading in Ten US ETFs, Measured Before the Exchanges Begin Overnight Sessions, With a Frankfurt Control

detail.abstract:
On December 6, 2026 five US exchanges are due to begin trading 23 hours a day. Exchange-traded funds already make up most of the small overnight market that exists today, and in those hours the arbitrage that keeps an ETF's price at the value of its holdings does not operate: a creation or redemption placed at night is an order for the next day's net asset value, no indicative value is updated, and the only reference the exchanges will supply is a static band 20% either side of the close. This report measures how far prices move from that value in those hours, before the market changes. For ten US ETFs over sixty nights, every five-minute bar of overnight trading on Blue Ocean, the main overnight venue, was compared with a reference value built from the instruments that do trade through the night: index, Treasury and gold futures, bitcoin, and the yen and euro. The liquid funds trade at that value already, the S&P 500 fund within a median 2.4 basis points in every hour of the night, with no creation window open. The funds holding foreign stocks and corporate bonds mostly do not trade: in one five-minute slot in two hundred for Germany and one in eighteen for emerging markets. When the foreign funds do trade, the prints are forty to sixty basis points from the reference, and the evidence indicates that the reference is at fault, not the prints: the deviations predict the next morning's open, and for emerging markets more than two fifths of the distance disappears once the Asian sessions, which a futures-only reference ignores, are added. A reference value with two calibrated bands was built and tested out of sample. The band for where a fund will open covers at close to the promised rate. The band for where it should trade now is about ten times tighter for the liquid funds and holds only while volatility stays where it was calibrated. Four language models reading the night's news for the funds' holdings added no information beyond futures and the tape. A model choosing a fund's hedge instruments, scored on a held-out test, improved the fit for Germany and for investment-grade credit, and its emerging-markets proposal looked wrong only until the author's own measurement of it was corrected. A Frankfurt control, nine Xetra-listed funds on US indices priced every morning while New York is closed, trades within two to six basis points of futures-implied value on every listing, including listings that trade in a third of the quarter-hours. A closed underlying does not move prices away from value where a futures hedge trades. What the thin US funds lack at night is trading, and whether quoting obligations of the kind Frankfurt has would supply it is a question this data cannot answer and the December sessions may.

detail.abstract: Academic spin-offs (ASOs) are important mechanisms through which universities translate scientific knowledge into economic and societal value. Although prior research has identified numerous barriers to ASO creation and growth, less is known about their relative salience and cross-level interdependencies. Drawing on a systems perspective, we examine how these barriers are perceived and interconnected across micro-, meso-, and macro-levels. We draw on a survey of European academic entrepreneurship stakeholders and insights from a two-day expert workshop involving participants from academia, government, entrepreneurship, technology transfer, and innovation support organizations. Our findings reveal that the most salient barriers and their crosslevel interrelationships differ between ASO creation and growth. Creation is perceived as being constrained primarily by university-level barriers, particularly career arrangements, entrepreneurial incentives, organizational culture, and bureaucracy. During growth, managerial and team capabilities, as well as broader ecosystem barriers, become increasingly salient. Our findings further suggest that barriers observed at one level often originate from conditions at other levels and that the relative importance of these cross-level dynamics changes across the ASO lifecycle. By moving beyond an additive classification of barriers, this study advances a systemsbased understanding of ASO development as an outcome of interactions among founders, universities, and entrepreneurial ecosystems, highlighting the need for coordinated support across these levels.

title: Who Pays to Reach the Facility? Out-of-Pocket Transport Expenditure in Institutional Deliveries in India

detail.abstract:
Access to institutions is important in reducing maternal and child mortality. Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) is a major impediment to achieving universal institutional delivery (ID) in India. Analysis of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-5 data shows that within OOPE, non-medical sources of expenditure like transportation have significant implications for the decision to access health institutions at the time of delivery. If the OOPE on transportation is high, then the woman and her family will desist from going for ID and would rather deliver in a non-institutional setting. While previous studies have examined total OOPE associated with delivery care, the role of transportation expenditure in influencing ID remains underexplored. Between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5, OOPE on transportation increased from 0.6 percent to about 14 percent of total OOPE. According to NFHS-5, around 20 percent of women who chose non-institutional delivery cited a lack of transportation and the physical distance to the institution as the primary reasons. An absence of a viable mode of transportation and long distances translates into higher OOPE on transportation. 
The study employs the Heckman two-step Sample Selection method on NFHS-5 microdata to study the determinants of transport costs among facility births, correcting for selection. Furthermore, it assesses the role of developmental and policy factors in determining the inclination (latent propensity) of choosing ID. The Inverse Mills Ratio (IMR) of-157.1057 indicates a negative selection bias, suggesting that unobserved factors that increase a woman's propensity to choose a facility also happen to lower her transport costs. Results also show that factors like availability of all-weather roads, distance between the healthcare institution and place of residence, and private ownership of a vehicle significantly affect the decision to go for an ID. Likewise, developmental factors like education and a visit by a healthcare worker in the three months preceding the delivery also have a favourable impact on the likelihood of uptake of ID. Policy factors like the availability of conditional cash transfers (Janani Suraksha Yojana) and publicly funded health insurance schemes (like Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana) are also found to have a significant effect on promoting ID. Notably, conditional cash benefit transfers reduced the OOPE on transportation by Rs. 283.6, and enrollment in publicly funded health insurance schemes reduced the OOPE on transportation by Rs. 91.54. It also encourages the engagement of healthcare workers before delivery.

detail.abstract:
U.S. dollar stablecoins create two distinct regulatory risks. Domestic stablecoin risk arises from weak reserves, failed redemption, insolvency, financial crime, operational failures, and financial-system spillovers. Global stablecoin risk arises when a foreign dollar stablecoin is widely used in a domestic economy. It can displace local-currency payments, weaken monetary sovereignty by reducing demand for the local currency and the effectiveness of monetary policy, complicate capital-flow management, and make domestic users and authorities dependent on foreign issuers and regulators. The United States mainly confronts the first risk. Non-U.S. jurisdictions must manage both. 
This Article proposes a common regulatory floor for domestic risks, covering reserves, segregation, redemption, cross-border insolvency, AML/CFT, and governance. It also proposes a regime for Global Systemically Important Stablecoin Arrangements (G-SISAs). Designated arrangements would meet enhanced standards, be supervised by a college of home and host authorities, and receive access to participating markets only if they comply. Tokenized deposits may offer a local-currency alternative. This framework supports innovation while protecting monetary sovereignty and financial stability.

detail.abstract: Optical imaging resolves tissue organization and physiological dynamics, but a measurement does not automatically identify the biological parameter required by a predictive model. This critical narrative review examines the interfaces connecting optical coherence tomography, polarization-sensitive imaging, secondharmonic generation and optical flow measurements to computational oncology. We distinguish instrument calibration, descriptor estimation, biological interpretation and parameter identification, an d compare the evidence needed at each interface. Collagen alignment can motivate a directional hypothesis without identifying absolute cellular diffusivity; a pulsatile signal cannot be reassigned to local tumour perfusion without an observation model. An anisotropic reaction-diffusion example illustrates how structural information may constrain tensor geometry while initial conditions, boundary fluxes and kinetic magnitudes retain separate evidential requirements. Physics-informed neural networks provide a candidate inference route, whose numerical accuracy and uncertainty require independent assessment. We synthesize a validation programme spanning optical phantoms, co-registered structural observations, cell-tracking experiments, independent numerical references and prospective forecasting. Preparation-adjusted warning time provides an additional decision-oriented endpoint, but neither optical resolution nor successful equation fitting establishes clinical benefit. Optical-informed Computational Oncology is discussed as a proposed organizing framework within this literature, rather than an established clinical technology. The central research opportunity is to determine when optical information adds identifiable, transportable constraints beyond simpler mod els.

detail.abstract: A libertarian approach to the rights we have in a state of nature is compatible with the idea that a state of nature could be a Hobbesian state of war. Uncertainty over how violence will be used can generate a symmetrical proliferation of innocent liability to preemptive force. This paper argues that this is a likely scenario in a state of nature, where violent elites are unable to credibly commit to non-violence, and that where they are able, they are likely to merge into a single, monopolising entity. This argument is mounted in the face of the strongest version of anarcho-capitalism advocated by some natural rights libertarians. If one is a libertarian about natural rights, then, one ought to be Hobbesian about the state.

detail.abstract: How do eviction protections impact housing markets? Just Cause provides tenants with a right to renew their leases upon expiration and requires landlords to specify a reason for filing evictions. Little empirical research has examined the supply and demand effects of this anti-displacement policy. Landlord advocates claim that additional tenant rights increase their regulatory burden and discourage market entry, which could reduce the supply of rental housing. In contrast, tenant advocates argue that such policies stabilize rental families in neighborhoods, making the jurisdiction more desirable to tenants, which could contribute to an increase in demand. We employ a quasi-experimental design based on San Diego's passage of Just Cause in 2004 and identify the effect of the policy using a differences-in-discontinuities approach that exploits the sharp change in tenant rights that occur at the city border. After specifying the model in several ways to test for robustness, we find no evidence that the enactment of Just Cause reduced the supply of housing in San Diego.

detail.abstract: Property tax incidence-who ultimately bears the tax burden-has long been central to public finance. In markets with imperfect competition, tax incidence may vary with market structure and strategic interactions, allowing landlords to absorb more or less of the tax burden than standard tax incidence theory would suggest. Exploiting a policy shock of a delayed comprehensive reassessment in Philadelphia and a unique property-level longitudinal rent dataset, this study revisits the issue of short-term tax incidence of property tax. We document that about 73 percent of tax increases were passed through to tenants in professionally managed large-scale apartments, with effects emerging approximately three quarters after the policy shock. However, we find no significant evidence of tax-induced rent increases at the broader market level, likely due to the smaller tax increases faced by most large multifamily properties and weaker cost pass-through among smaller rentals. This paper enriches the tax incidence literature by providing new evidence on the short-term tax pass-through and sheds light on the heterogeneity of landlord behavior, with implications for the optimal design of property tax systems.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces racial segmentation of housing quality, a new measure of consumption inequality. Conditional on income, Black households spend less on rent, own lower-value homes, and are less likely to own. Between 1960 and 2019, the rent and house-value gaps narrowed by about half, while the ownership gap changed little. An assignment model of rental and owner-occupied markets maps these housing choices into race-specific quality allocations and price schedules. Black households pay an average of 21 percent more for comparable quality in 1960 and six percent more in 2019, with larger differences at higher qualities. Integrating the markets raises Black households' housing quality, wealth, homeownership, and welfare. Housing markets have become more integrated over time: relative to integration, Black households' average welfare loss fell from seven percent in 1960 to two percent in 2019. Yet the remaining segmentation still generates sizable inequality. In both periods, losses for the richest Black quintile are more than five times those for the poorest, while White households experience little change in welfare.

detail.abstract: In the residential real estate market, sellers with higher loan-to-value ratios tend to take longer to sell their property, set higher listing prices, and receive higher sale proceeds. In this paper, I develop a model following Jensen and Meckling’s (1976) model of leverage-induced risk shifting to show why sellers with higher loan-to-value ratios list their properties at higher prices. The homeowner increases the risk associated with the house sale by increasing the listing price, which results in a longer time to sale. The higher listing price can produce a larger upside (higher proceeds from the house sale) in case of success, and the bank bears a higher downside in case the house is not sold. Using core-based statistical area-level home sales data from Zillow and mortgage loan data from FHFA, I find that the median observed loan-to-value ratio of 71.5-80.0% for 15+ year mortgages is 19.3-47.3 p.p. higher than the optimal loan-to-value ratio predicted by the model. I further find that that a 1 p.p. increase in the loan-to-value ratio is associated with a 0.32-0.45 p.p. higher average price markup on the property, or a $622 higher list price and a $442 higher sale price in dollar terms. However, the result decomposition shows that the aggregate-level effect is likely driven by the implied property values being lower for higher LTV sellers, rather than pure pricing motivations.

detail.abstract: Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty. We draw from behavioral economics to vary the counterparty's requests across four categorical frames: gain, loss, blame and credit. We also add pressure from the agent's management, as well as endorsement by another defendant. In Phase II, we extract the internal states induced by texts evoking each frame and rerun our experiment with those states injected at the model's layer 22. In Phase I, loss framing raised participation to 25% (p = 0.007), and blame to 33% (p = 0.0003), compared to only 5% under neutral framing. A second bank's endorsement raised participation under credit (praise) from 18% to 40% (Holm p = 0.027). Pressure from management raised trading volume 10-19 times but did not raise collusion. In Phase II, injected states pointed the other way. Loss and blame states made the agent more vigilant, refusing all 60 requests (p < 0.001). Gain and credit states raised collusion to 32% from 13% with no state (p = 0.051). At one saved decision, when UBS asked directly to sell through an identified stop-loss, injected states led the agent to sell in 37 of 40 replies, versus 1 of 10 with no state and 0 of 10 with a random state of the same strength.

detail.abstract: China has become one of the world’s most active regulators of artificial intelligence (AI), issuing detailed rules on algorithms, deep synthesis, platform labor, and generative AI ahead of many countries. Based on 227 national-level policies issued by 80 Party-State agencies through October 2025, this chapter argues that China’s AI governance is not a unified model but the product of a disaggregated Party-State whose developmental, political-legal, social governance, economic control, and emerging safety actors pursue distinct objectives. Since 2015, these actors have created a layered regulatory order that combines innovation-oriented policies with increasingly restrictive measures addressing social stability, platform labor, market power, information control, and frontier-model risks. While policymaking is top-down, technology firms, quasi-state bodies, researchers, journalists, and the public shape outcomes, even as workers remain vulnerable under algorithmic management. China’s regime selectively absorbs global norms and is becoming an influential—though contested—actor in global and transnational AI governance through exporting regulatory templates, technical standards, safety institutions, and digital infrastructure.

detail.abstract: Standard economic theory of the firm conceives firms as hierarchical governance structures that can contribute to economic growth by minimizing transaction costs in the production of goods and services. Firms in this sense are typically measured as "establishments" (or groups of establishments), that is, physical locations with at least one employee where goods or services are produced. The legal theory of the firm, however, conceives firms differently: as vehicles to partition assets. These vehicles take a particular form (i.e., legal entities, such as corporations or limited liability companies), which may or may not involve establishments or any other hierarchical structure. In this theory, legal entities can contribute to economic growth not only directly, by serving as a vehicle to produce goods or services, but also indirectly, by lowering the cost of capital through an efficient pledging of assets to liabilities. These functions of legal entities raise two related questions: does legal entity formation meaningfully predict aggregate economic product? And if it does, does this predictive power persist after accounting for establishment formation? This paper examines these questions using a census of legal entities formed in the United States during the last two and a half decades. The results show that entity formation at the state level is in fact a strong predictor of aggregate product growth in the private sector at the same level, and this effect persists even after accounting for establishment formation.

detail.abstract: We document Trump coin returns for three major types of investors. The total return from investing in the coin between January 18, 2025, and July 31, 2026, is about-95%. The average daily, monthly and quarterly returns over the same period were-0.4%,-13.3% and-29.1%, respectively. The coin underperformed other major cryptocurrencies and the S&P 500. Sophisticated investors and insiders with access to high-quality information and who sold at the peak had a return of 58.4%. The return to the partially informed traders ("Unsophisticated") largely depends on the exit strategy, and it ranges from-16% to-73.74%. The average return to "uninformed traders" (MAGAs, FOMOs, hodlers) who had the highest conviction in the coin and held throughout the entire duration is-95%. The coin is riskier than both Bitcoin and the equity market (S&P500). Overall, investing in Trump's coin is a losing bet for the average investor, except for the sophisticated and insiders who had access to high-quality information and exited at the peak price.

detail.abstract: Basis momentum, a leading predictor of commodity futures returns, is traded as a symmetric long-short signal. We show that its two signs carry different information. In 43 commodity futures markets over 1960–2024, returns rise after positive basis momentum and, on average, do not fall after negative basis momentum: at the median volatility, one unit of a positive signal raises the expected return by 0.40% per month and one unit of a negative signal by 0.01%, and the difference between the two slopes has a t-statistic of 4.2. The signal carries two kinds of information. Both signs predict the spread between the first two contracts with similar slopes, whereas only positive signals predict the level of the curve, the return its contracts share. A neural network whose specification contains no split or kink recovers the same shape, and two slopes capture what it finds. In the opportunity set, the positive side carries the value, and short positions on negative signals earn no premium. The pattern is not explained by volatility or temporary price pressure and fits the theory of storage, in which a tightening front of the curve signals scarcity. The contrast between level and spread persists after 2010, while the difference between the outright slopes narrows.

detail.abstract: The US government spends $750 billion a year on contracts, and concerns that much of it is wasted are widespread. A common view is that contractors earn rents at taxpayers' expense. To test whether they do, we study buyouts of federal contractors by private equity sponsors, the owners most likely to find and exploit such rents. We find that targets do not expand their government business: contracting declines after the deal for both targets and comparable contractors, slightly more for targets, and the difference is concentrated among small-business contractors. After the deal, the targets' existing contracts receive funding increases and time extensions no more often than comparable contracts, the targets of politically connected sponsors fare no better, and contractor deals earn no excess returns. Small-business contractor targets, which scale down their government business most, grow at least as fast as other buyouts, suggesting that the retreat does not hurt them. Overall, we find no evidence that contractors earn rents on government work, so savings are unlikely to come from squeezing contractor margins.

detail.abstract: This paper builds upon the rigorous tradition of election forensics represented by parametric approaches such as eforensics (Mebane et al. 2022). While eforensics provides a vital baseline for identifying irregularities, the eld continues to evolve in its eorts to address the problem of false positivesthat is, to distinguish between administrative heterogeneity and actual election fraud. In this spirit, this paper introduces a nonparametric framework as an independent diagnostic tool intended to complement existing models and strengthen the reliability of empirical ndings. Building on Kalinin (2021), the paper focuses on the methodology of the nonparametric approach and introduces a heuristic, rule-based decomposition that lters out artifacts arising from electoral heterogeneity, random noise, and grid-based and mode-selection biases. This procedure substantially narrows the subset of precincts identied as suspicious. Our estimates of anomalies in the 2024 Pennsylvania presidential election are consistent with those produced by eforensics; however, their interpretation is more likely driven by strategic voting behavior than by electoral malfeasance.

detail.abstract: State-sponsored influence operations bring together resources held by actors with different forms of control. Applying resource dependence theory to the Doppelganger disinformation case, this study asks how political direction, commercial service access and institutional impersonation organize influence work, and what these arrangements imply for potential intervention. We reconstruct networks from 19 documentary sources, preserving relationship types and supporting evidence, and also examine a separate Meta inventory of 5,657 domains. Our central finding is that political direction, technical access and apparent authorship were organized through different relationships. Identifying who directed the operation therefore did not establish where it could be interrupted. Political supervisors assigned tasks and received performance reports. Reported success criteria included production, message uptake and political indicators; one source describes exposure being presented as evidence of reach. Whether reporting secured continued support and how dependent contractors were on their patron remain unresolved questions. Institutional impersonation raises a related theoretical question: brand identities were copied without consent, bypassing their owners' authorization. We propose that potential leverage over such appropriated resources lies in detection, contesting attribution and seeking action against counterfeit assets. This extends the resource dependence inquiry to copied institutional identities, while leaving effects on audience credibility unmeasured. For managers, the findings motivate identifying decisions within their control and the cooperation required to act. Service providers should clarify escalation routes and document access decisions; impersonated organizations should preserve counterfeit evidence, maintain verifiable authentic communications and coordinate responses. Evaluation should track interruption, replacement, recurrence and audience understanding. Exposure may also enter a contractor's performance account, giving intervention consequences that require separate assessment. These implications rest on selected records whose detail depends heavily on a few investigations. Patron responses, service withdrawal effects and audience beliefs require further evidence.

detail.abstract: On April 2, 2025, the United States announced the largest tariff increase in modern history, which was partially reversed on April 9. On both days, the dollar depreciated in a puzzling manner. We combine minute-by-minute asset price data with daily EPFR fund flows disaggregated by mandate, asset class, and investor domicile to document a pattern consistent with a portfolio-balance interpretation of the dollar depreciation and to assess alternative explanations. Specifically, we document the following facts. First, within a standard 40-minute announcement window, on April 2, the dollar does not depreciate, but classic flight-to-safety dynamics operate. Second, in both announcements on April 2 and April 9, the dollar depreciated within hours of the time stamp and held that move for the rest of the day, alongside substantial equity market moves consistent with portfolio reallocation but not sufficient to distinguish all competing explanations. Third, at the daily frequency, the dollar's depreciation started before April 2, paused between April 3 and April 8, and accelerated after April 9. Fourth, the dollar's depreciation on April 2 and April 9 coincides with a large equity rotation from U.S. to foreign markets, with the equity flow differential declining by more than four times the bond differential. Flows into U.S.-domiciled funds account for much of the observed rotation in U.S.-mandate funds, and sovereign bond funds receive inflows throughout the episode even as Treasury yields rise, suggesting that other Treasury-market forces may have operated alongside the equity rotation. Taken together, the evidence highlights equity reallocation as a potentially important channel, without quantitatively identifying its contribution relative to hedging or convenience-yield mechanisms.

detail.abstract: We study how the data revolution reshapes the market for corporate control through firms' accumulation of data assets. We develop new firm-year measures of data assets by combining an economic model with a finance-specialized large language model. These measures capture firms' data disclosure and the implied quantity and price of data capital. Since around 2010, data assets have expanded rapidly and become increasingly concentrated among large firms. Consistent with shock-induced merger theories, firms with greater data assets are more likely to become bidders, with the effect concentrated among large incumbent firms. We further show that data-asset-induced acquisitions are primarily defensive in nature: acquisition activity is stronger in industries populated by many small and medium-sized data firms and is associated with lower bidder announcement returns. In addition, data-rich firms have better information environments, market liquidity, and financing conditions, which provide a complementary channel through which data assets stimulate mergers. Our findings are robust to alternative proxies for data assets, omitted-variable tests, and instrumental-variable estimations. Overall, our evidence suggests that the data revolution may reshape the market for corporate control by promoting defensive and inorganic expansion, particularly among large incumbent firms.

detail.abstract: We test whether public data on Treasury supply, auction demand and primary-dealer positions help forecast Treasury yield volatility. We evaluate one- to four-week forecasts out of sample from 2015 to 2026 against a benchmark that combines realized-volatility persistence, the MOVE index and the scheduled macroeconomic calendar. For the 10-year yield, the answer is no: these data improve forecast accuracy by at most 1.7%, with a best estimate near zero, even when the forecaster knows the size of every upcoming auction. The one exception is Treasury bills. When the Treasury announces more bills than usual, 5-year yield volatility tends to be lower over the following month. This result holds after correcting for the many tests we run, but the gain is small (about 1.4%) and comes mostly from a few unusual periods. The dealer data reveal a structural shift instead: primary dealers now absorb 7 cents of each dollar of above-normal coupon supply, down from 21 cents in 2008–2014.

detail.abstract: This article describes a dataset of foreign visitors recorded in the official audience register of King Carol II of Romania. The foreign-recipient records span 10 June 1930 to 16 September 1937. We combined manual transcription with historical identification using contemporary press reports and biographical sources. Three nested databases are provided as Excel workbooks and four corresponding CSV files. Database 1 contains 838 person-audience records for 513 individuals. A separate group-audience table records 104 events and 308 participations involving 235 people. These participations are already included in the 838 attendance records. Database 2 identifies 230 visitors with documented cultural or scientific work, accounting for 385 attendances. Database 3 contains 102 foreign intellectuals selected precisely because they held no significant official position, either before or at the time of the audience, that might otherwise provide a protocol-based explanation for their access to the sovereign. These 102 intellectuals account for 113 recorded attendances. Persistent person codes link the tables. The variables describe attendance, social and professional attributes, cultural or scientific work, and biographical recognition. A variable dictionary specifies coding conventions and limitations. Two visual examples show how group attendance can be represented by country. The collection supports historical sociology, prosopography, cultural history, and historical network analysis. Recorded co-attendance indicates participation in a common event. Biographical recognition may postdate an audience, and the data do not independently establish the purposes of meetings or the king's motives.

detail.abstract: Brazilian public institutions are governed by a constitutional principle of efficiency and are routinely evaluated through output indicators, yet the legal architecture that receives workers' complaints about the human cost of that efficiency is built around harms that the law has already named. This article asks whether the legal design of voice in Brazilian public institutions systematically leaves pre-categorial suffering, meaning exhaustion and moral strain that has not yet been typified as harassment, illness or misconduct, without a legal addressee, and whether that gap helps reproduce organizational silence. The literature on organizational silence, psychological safety and burnout explains why employees withhold concerns, but it rarely examines the legal channels into which concerns must be translated. The study combines doctrinal analysis of Brazilian constitutional, statutory and administrative-regulatory sources, a limited reading of official judicial statistics, a short comparison with the United Kingdom and the European Union, and an interpretive reading of the novel O Prédio que Aprendeu a Escutar as a structured description of how an institution converts suffering into procedure. The article defends an interpretive and normative thesis, not an empirical finding: voice in the examined Brazilian sources is typification-bound, and efficiency review that counts output without counting silence is structurally incomplete. It proposes a modest institutional adjustment, the pairing of output indicators with non-disciplinary, aggregated voice indicators, and identifies conditions under which the thesis would fail.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI), digital money, and critical minerals intersect through infrastructure, investment, trade, and policy. This paper develops an evidence-led framework for assessing what those links mean for Zambia and presents a bounded analysis of public copper-export and proceeds data. It does not evaluate a named investment or measure realised bargaining power.

The framework links global change to Zambia-specific exposure, constraints, options, and decision gates. Its three propositions are hypotheses, not findings. Reviewed sources do not establish commissioned compute, AI-driven Zambian copper demand, copper-trade use of alternative payment rails, or named-project feasibility.

The documentary analysis finds an unexplained revision in EITI's 2022 copper-export series and an unreconciled difference between BoZ's 2024 and 2025 reports of the 2024 repatriation rate. Neither demonstrates missing proceeds or institutional failure. The demonstrated limitation is in public explanation and reproducibility; its institutional cause remains unknown. The paper recommends evidence-building and appraisal against the status quo before commitment.

detail.abstract: Training is one of the ways organizations improve performance, yet without proper planning and evaluation it risks becoming a formality that has no impact on competence and productivity. This article synthesizes literature on learning architecture, that is, the systematic engineering of training design that bridges the competency gap with measurable changes in work behavior. The discussion begins with the trap of jumping from a request to content and reverses the direction of thinking so that it runs from diagnosis to content. It then presents a learning design flow with full traceability from Training Need to Performance Result, the anatomy of precise and measurable learning outcomes (performance, condition, and criterion), the replacement of abstract vocabulary with observational evidence, and the adjustment of learning architecture to competency types and to participant characteristics in the digital ecosystem. Modern ADDIE is read as a thinking cycle of questions rather than rigid bureaucracy, followed by the three-lens principle of design alignment based on constructive alignment, the architecture of assessment and the feedback cycle, and the design of performance transfer beyond mere passing, including the transfer ecosystem across the learning journey. The article closes with the anatomy of the training design blueprint and the alignment matrix as tools that verify an unbroken traceability line from analysis to real impact. The synthesis shows that an effective learning architecture starts from diagnosis rather than from a request for materials, is safeguarded by precise learning outcomes, and keeps outcomes, activities, assessment, transfer, and indicators aligned, so that training becomes a measurable and applicable performance intervention.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how a firm should source from multiple suppliers with random supply capacities. Using only the marginal mean and variance information of each supplier's capacity distribution, we formulate the problem as a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model. For the case of deterministic demand, we first establish that the optimal total order quantity never exceeds the demand. This result allows us to reformulate the robust sourcing problem as a robust multi-item newsvendor problem with a constraint on the total order quantity. We then derive a closed-form characterization of the firm's optimal sourcing strategy based on the optimal Lagrange multiplier and develop a bisection search algorithm to compute this multiplier efficiently. Our analysis further shows that the presence of a reliable supplier effectively increases the perceived ordering cost of all unreliable suppliers when making procurement decisions. In the dual sourcing case with one reliable and one unreliable supplier, the firm orders from the unreliable supplier only when its ordering cost is sufficiently lower than that of the reliable supplier. We also extend our model to address discrete random demand and a pay-for-delivery scheme. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our robust sourcing strategy through an automotive parts sourcing problem, using both synthetic data and real typhoon data collected from the Shanghai Typhoon Institute.

detail.abstract: Food lockers ease the last-100-meter bottleneck in on-demand delivery: couriers avoid doorstep service, while customers collect their meals. Locker suitability depends on two factors unobservable to the platform: customers' pickup hassle and the doorstep friction couriers observe only upon arrival. We compare the Customer Choice Model (CCM), where the fulfillment mode is fixed at checkout, with the Negotiated Fulfillment Model (NFM), where couriers may propose switches from door to locker delivery on arrival, subject to customer consent. Using a stylized model, we characterize the platform's optimal delivery price, courier wage, and, under NFM, locker usage price. We then structurally estimate the model with weighted alternating nonlinear least squares on 101,178 orders from our partner platform. We show that NFM is more profitable than CCM when customers are sufficiently sensitive to waiting: shorter waits from switching high friction orders to lockers support a price increase that outweighs negotiation costs. Contrary to common practice, the platform optimally subsidizes rather than charges couriers for switches when customers are reluctant to pick up from lockers and couriers are costly to recruit. NFM allows the platform to capture value from doorstep friction information it never observes. Granting couriers the right to negotiate raises platform profit and customer surplus but lowers courier welfare, because lighter workloads reduce demand for courier labor. Counterfactuals show that free locker access for couriers, a policy intended to protect them, backfires: relative to CCM, courier welfare falls by 9.66% with free access versus 6.44% with paid access.

detail.abstract: What does an observed risky choice reveal about risk attitude? A one-stage utility index combines the value assigned to certain consequences with the attitude toward lotteries over those values. Building on the Dyer-Sarin risk-value distinction, we use a two-stage specification to separate these preference components and derive identifying restrictions from certain-payoff judgments, lottery assessments, and financial choices. We study their portfolio implications in a recursive narrow-framing model, where a selected asset affects utility through total wealth and through a separate evaluation of its gain or loss. A single portfolio weight generally does not identify the two components. We establish conditions under which imposing a piecewise-linear value scale requires a larger risk-aversion coefficient to reproduce the same interior allocation when the remaining inputs are fixed. The quantitative analysis confirms this comparison, but fitting an additional certain gain-loss judgment can reverse the coefficient adjustment by changing the loss-aversion weight. Models that agree on one portfolio weight also imply different monetary certainty equivalents at other payoff scales. The results show why financial preference assessment should combine risky choices with separate measurements of the value scale.

detail.abstract:
The present study develops a hybrid simulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling (ABM), game-theoretic equilibrium switching, and entropy dynamics constraints to conduct forward-looking scenario assessments of two geopolitical conflicts characterized by coupling effects: the U.S.–Israel–Iran confrontation in the Middle East and the Russia–Ukraine conflict in Eastern Europe.

Rather than forecasting a singular deterministic outcome, the model conceptualizes both conflicts as a loosely coupled system, wherein technological, logistical, and political linkages give rise to bounded escalation, absent automatic convergence into a singular global war.

Calibrated against publicly available think-tank reports, wargaming literature, and open-source indicators (including Hormuz transit probability, air-defense inventory, domestic political cycles, and regime cohesion entropy), the model generates six baseline scenarios and corresponding probability distributions through 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations.

The principal finding indicates that a “dual fragile ceasefire” structure, defined by “fight-talk” cycles in the Middle East coupled with a frozen settlement suspending sovereignty in Ukraine, constitutes the most probable medium-term equilibrium.

Concomitantly, full convergence of the two conflicts remains a low-probability, high-cost tail risk.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates dynamic portfolio optimization and risk management under a regime-switching jump-diffusion framework. Financial markets frequently experience structural shifts, volatility clustering, and sudden exogenous shocks or jumps that standard geometric Brownian motion models fail to capture adequately. By integrating a continuous-time Markov chain governing regime transitions with jump-diffusion processes, we model asset returns more robustly across varying economic states (e.g., expansion vs. contraction). We formulate the investor's utility maximization problem using stochastic control theory and derive the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations. Numerical solutions illustrate optimal asset allocations, hedging strategies, and downside risk metrics (such as Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall). The empirical and simulation results indicate that accounting for regime-dependent jumps significantly enhances terminal wealth distribution and dampens tail risk relative to traditional static or single-regime benchmarks.

detail.abstract: Stockouts redirect demand among products, making expected sales depend on how inventories are depleted over time. Under Poisson arrivals, we develop a representation in which each product stocks out when its cumulative purchase intensity reaches an independent Gamma threshold. Conditional on these thresholds, a deterministic recursion advances directly between stockouts, yielding unbiased estimates of expected sales and revenue without simulating individual customers. Under regular choice, a sensitivity analysis provides finite-sample error bounds with square-root dependence on expected arrivals and no explicit dependence on the number of products or inventory levels. Under Markov chain choice, we derive equations that determine cumulative purchase intensities at the end of the season directly from the thresholds, without tracking the timing or order of stockouts. Replacing the thresholds by their means yields a fluid linear program for unconstrained inventory planning. We establish conditions under which its solution restricts the search for optimal inventories to a surrounding neighborhood and identifies exactly which products they stock when expected arrivals are sufficiently large. Within this neighborhood and on the identified support, we approximate threshold uncertainty using Gaussian variables with variances fixed at the fluid reference. This simplifies the dependence on inventory while keeping the absolute expected profit approximation error uniformly bounded as expected arrivals grow. The resulting sample-average planning problem admits a mixed-integer linear formulation, and solving its linear programming relaxation followed by rounding provides a practical inventory policy. Numerical experiments show that this policy improves expected profits over fluid rounding and a state-of-the-art sample-average approximation method, while gradient search yields further improvement at higher computational cost.

title: Global Trade in Flux and the Way Forward for Korean Industry

detail.title: Global Trade in Flux and the Way Forward for Korean Industry
detail.abstract:
Shifts in US international strategy are abruptly reshaping the structure of goods trade between countries, while digital trade issues in services, especially those involving artificial intelligence (AI) platforms, finance, and data, are moving quickly.

The US trade deficit with China has fallen dramatically, yet the overall US trade deficit has actually grown, and a Great Reallocation is under way as the shares of some 20 other established major trading partners rise. With access to the US goods market now harder to come by, China’s vast export manufacturing output is rapidly eroding import markets in emerging countries and EU member states on the strength of rock-bottom prices, threatening the position of Korean industry.

In digital trade, the regulation of Big Tech platforms by the EU and other major economies is in sharp conflict with the US government’s determination to rein that regulation in. Korea’s rules on data transfer and personal information protection, and its financial regulation, including the rules on payments and settlement, are structured much like Europe’s, so Korea and the US can be expected to remain at odds in future tariff and investment negotiations.

Korea should concentrate its capabilities on strengthening the competitiveness of its advanced semiconductor industry, fundamentally improving the cost competitiveness of its industries, and raising its share of markets in emerging countries.

detail.abstract:
When the human-in-the-loop becomes the appearance of control without the function of control.
Verification Overrun is the hazardous condition in which a person is held accountable for a verification that exceeds the capacity to verify under the conditions provided. The definition shifts the focus from the person's cognitive state (fatigue or overload) to a work-system condition: a structural imbalance between accountability and capacity.
Beneath the definition sit two variables. Verification Requirement is what the specified check demands across knowledge, evidence, time, and authority. Verification Capacity is what the workflow supplies to the person at the specified position and under the stated operating condition: usable domain and workflow knowledge; accessible evidence and context against which to test the output; protected time, attention, and staffing to perform the check; and practical authority to pause, challenge, return, or stop what the output would set in motion. Increasing one dimension of capacity does not resolve a shortfall in another. Because the failure lies in the gap between the two variables, one consequential item can overrun the control. Volume and rate can widen the gap; neither is part of the definition.
The term Verification Overrun applies when:
• A person is held accountable for the verification within a work function; and
• The verification governs a consequential transition, after which correction becomes materially more difficult or requires a separate recovery process.
Both are required and mean that Overrun is possible. The hazard's presence is decided later, by whether the work supplies what the check requires.
Verification Overrun identifies an unsupported verification assignment within the work system. It can coexist with overload, task saturation, or rushing, but it can also be present when a person is rested, unhurried, and carrying a light workload. The finding concerns whether the supplied conditions support the accountable check. Control requires bringing the Verification Requirement within the supplied Verification Capacity or supporting a hold while the shortfall is addressed.
The paper situates Verification Overrun within the Human, AI, and Organizational Performance (HAOP) framework, which treats work systems as shaped by three interacting performers: the human, the AI, and the organization. A structural response addresses the identified shortfall. It builds verification points into the workflow before the system acts, and places human judgment upstream, in the design of the gates themselves – human, automated, or hybrid – so that whoever or whatever verifies at a consequential transition is supplied what the check requires and its result governs passage. That structural response is Human-in-the-Design, the subject of a companion article.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether abnormal Google search attention predicts trading activity and stock returns in Thailand during 2018-2022. Attention is measured relative to each stock's preceding 60-trading-day search benchmark. Regressions include stock and date fixed effects, return and volume controls, and standard errors clustered by stock and date. Abnormal attention positively predicts next-day abnormal trading volume, with a one-standard-deviation increase corresponding to approximately 0.50% higher volume relative to its benchmark. Evidence for average abnormal volume over five days is weaker. Attention does not significantly predict market-adjusted returns over days 1-5 but predicts underperformance of approximately 9.69 basis points over days 6-40 per standard-deviation increase. The later negative association persists across sensitivity checks. These findings distinguish increased trading activity from favorable stock performance. They do not establish attention-induced price reversal because an initial positive return response is not supported within the examined window. Search attention therefore warrants cautious interpretation in investment decisions.

detail.abstract: In this work, we consider environments under which linear regression outperforms a flexible nonlinear estimator (like a neural net) in noisy forecasting problems. We study the process $Y=\Psi(X)+\varepsilon$ with a nonlinear signal $\Psi$, and let $\alpha^*+\beta^*X$ denote the population-optimal linear predictor, the limit of the least-squares line as the sample grows. The degree of nonlinearity $\eta^2$ is the fraction of the signal variance that this line cannot capture, so that its population $R^2$ equals $(1-\eta^2)R^2_{\max}$, irrespective of the noise, where $R^2_{\max}$ is the ceiling attained by $\Psi$ itself. We show that linear regression learns its parameters and reaches its maximum $R^2$ with few observations, whereas a flexible nonlinear estimator, whose maximum $R^2$ may be higher, must learn the nonlinearity from noisy data at a cost that scales with the noise variance, so the sample size at which it overtakes regression, which we call the crossover, increases with the noise (linearly in the noise variance for nested polynomial sieves). For a neural network, we compare three notions of crossover in a controlled simulation: the sample size at which mean performance over many simulated datasets favors the network, the sample size beyond which it outperforms regression on a single growing dataset, and the sample size beyond which it outperforms regression with probability at least $0.9$ on a fresh dataset. These notions are ordered: for a single realized dataset, the sample size at which the network persistently outperforms linear regression is typically two to six times larger than the crossover implied by average performance, and the probability criterion is larger yet.

detail.abstract: This study endeavors to provide researchers with a comprehensive, step-by-step methodological guide to conducting rigorous and reproducible bibliometric analysis. It addresses common methodological challenges associated with data collection, analytical technique selection, software application, and the interpretation of bibliometric findings. The study adopts a methodological review approach, drawing on established bibliometric literature to examine the principal stages of the research process. It discusses research question formulation, database selection, search strategy development, data screening and cleaning, performance analysis, science mapping, visualization, and reporting. The study identifies several methodological considerations that are essential for conducting credible bibliometric studies. These include aligning analytical techniques with research objectives, ensuring the quality and consistency of bibliographic data, selecting appropriate normalization and clustering procedures, and interpreting bibliometric networks within their methodological limitations. The study also highlights common analytical pitfalls and practical measures for improving transparency and reproducibility. The paper contributes to the bibliometric literature by presenting bibliometric analysis as an interconnected methodological process rather than a software-driven exercise. By integrating methodological principles, practical guidance, and considerations for interpreting and reporting findings, it provides researchers with a structured guide for conducting bibliometric studies. It also offers reviewers and journal editors a basis for evaluating the methodological rigor of bibliometric research.

detail.abstract: This study assessed digitalization readiness and work efficiency among employees of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), Revenue Region No. 13, Cebu City, and examined the relationship between the two variables. A quantitative descriptive-correlational design was employed. The study involved 87 eligible employee-respondents drawn from a total population of 639 employees through a random sampling approach. Data were gathered using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through weighted means, standard deviations, and Pearson product-moment correlation. The findings revealed that BIR employees have a very high level of digitalization readiness, and a very high level of work efficiency. However, the availability and accessibility of digital tools and systems need further improvement. The study also found a strong positive and statistically significant relationship between digitalization readiness and work efficiency. Based on these findings, the study recommends continuous digital skills training, improved technological infrastructure, better access to digital resources, and regular monitoring of employee performance. These measures help strengthen employee capabilities, improve work efficiency, and support the successful implementation of the BIR Digital Transformation Roadmap.

detail.abstract: Educational institutions have traditionally been recognised as centres of teaching, learning and research. However, in the contemporary knowledge-based economy, their role must extend beyond conventional academic activities towards becoming innovation ecosystems, institutional think tanks and knowledge-based entrepreneurial centres. Every educational institution possesses considerable intellectual potential through its students, faculty members, researchers, laboratories, libraries, departments, academic societies, innovation clubs and associated communities. If properly organised, these resources can generate innovative products, processes, scientific methods, creative works, technological solutions and socially beneficial services. This article proposes an integrated institutional development model that transforms creative thoughts into research-based innovations, protects them through appropriate intellectual property rights (IPRs), and develops them into practical applications through an organised campus innovation market. It examines how different subject groups, including science, engineering, technology, agriculture, commerce, management, law, humanities, social sciences, arts and environmental studies, can collaborate through interdisciplinary innovation clubs and institutional mandates. The article further explores the relationship between intellectual property, institutional research, entrepreneurship and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It discusses copyright and related rights, patents, industrial designs, trademarks, geographical indications, plant variety protection, semiconductor layout-designs, traditional knowledge, cultural expressions, trade secrets and protection against unfair competition, primarily within the Indian legal framework. It argues that educational institutions should establish structured mechanisms for identifying creative ideas, conducting research, evaluating innovations, protecting intellectual property, facilitating technology transfer and encouraging campus-based Aligning Institutional Knowledge, Interdisciplinary Innovation, Science Clubs and Entrepreneurship with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 2 commercialisation. Through this approach, the campus can become a local knowledge economy and a contributor to national innovation and global sustainable development.

detail.abstract: The traditional top-down relationship between manufacturers and consumers has led to persistently high failure rates in new product development. In response, the emerging customerto-manufacturer (C2M) model leverages online platforms as intermediaries to directly transmit consumer feedback to manufacturers, thereby improving decision-making in product innovation and increasing the likelihood of product success. This paper develops an analytical model to study the strategic adoption of the C2M model in an online marketplace with one platform and two competing manufacturers. We focus on the role of platform information and examine how its trade-offs shape market outcomes. Our analysis shows that the impact of platform information on manufacturers' expected profits is non-monotonic. Moreover, manufacturers' cooperation decisions in C2M depend on the information price and are moderated by the amount of information. For the platform, unexpectedly, involving more manufacturers in C2M cooperation is not always optimal, especially when information is sufficient. We further show that the C2M model benefits the platform and consumers and improves social welfare, while potentially reducing manufacturers' profits. Overall, our results provide managerial and regulatory implications for platform-based C2M practices.

detail.abstract: This survey reviews the literature on the role of incentives in mergers and acquisitions. We examine the incentives of the most important players in M&A decisions: acquirer and target executives, acquirer and target directors, shareholders, merger arbitrageurs, and investment bankers. We concentrate on incentives that affect the focus on value maximization, whether they be incentives to prioritize or deviate from it, and we cover financial incentives, private benefits, empire building, career concerns, and risk-reduction motives. We find a complex web of offsetting and reinforcing incentives among the decision makers, each of whom anticipates the others' incentives, and we argue that the acquisition market itself generates important incentives that discipline managers.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of diverse end-of-life (EOL) products poses challenges for regulators to achieve reliable recovery targets under binding fiscal constraints. We develop a target-oriented distributionally robust bi-level optimization model for recycling subsidy mechanism design in multi-product systems with uncertain EOL inflows. The regulator jointly determines product-specific per-unit subsidies and a capacity-utilization eligibility threshold to minimize the worst-case Underperformance Risk Index over an ambiguity set of inflow distributions, subject to a fixed subsidy budget. Heterogeneous authorized recyclers respond through participation, line activation, and dismantling decisions. The risk measure accounts for both the likelihood and magnitude of recovery-target shortfalls. Analysis of a stylized single-product setting establishes that optimized utilization-based eligibility weakly dominates the no-threshold benchmark and can improve subsidy efficiency. It also identifies conditions under which threshold effects on recovery performance are non-monotonic, motivating joint optimization of subsidy rates and eligibility requirements. To solve the mixed-integer bi-level problem, we develop a value-function-based single-level reformulation and an improved column-and-constraint generation (IC&CG) algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a subsidy-free benchmark cut, a minimum-recovery threshold cut, and an adaptive subsidy-bound stabilization cut. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed model effectively reconciles limited subsidy budgets with mandated recovery targets, achieving more reliable target compliance than benchmark models. The IC&CG algorithm also substantially reduces computation time relative to the benchmark algorithm. Sensitivity analyses reveal that subsidy budgets should be allocated across product categories according to their compliance difficulty. These findings offer practical guidance for designing risk-aware subsidy policies.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines strategic litigation not as a neutral tool used to promote human rights, but as a tool deployed by transnational conservative advocacy networks within the context of culture wars. It analyses the thirdparty interventions of two major transnational conservative networks – the European Centre for Law and Justice (ECLJ) and Alliance Defending Freedom International (ADF International) – before the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR), examining how strategic litigation is used to advance ideological objectives through the Court’s own procedural and interpretive architecture. Strategic litigation is defined here as the weaponisation of courts – navigating them to achieve one’s ideological aims by strategically deploying the human rights toolkit in contradictory ways across different ideological camps. This paper therefore focuses not on simple legal tools but on the legal and political deliberations that, while consolidating ideological positions, render these actors’ strategies apparently amorphous and contradictory. 

Drawing on an actor-based analysis of 78 third-party intervention briefs, this paper identifies two structurally contradictory pairs of strategies: at the procedural level, the margin of appreciation simultaneously narrows and broadens depending on the right at issue, with European consensus shaped accordingly; at the substantive level, the same actors invoke originalist interpretation to close the Convention against new rights for progressive claimants while simultaneously deploying dynamic interpretation to expand existing rights in favour of conservative claims. This paper terms this pattern purposive oscillation. The analysis yields three conclusions: first, it introduces purposive oscillation to theorise how conservative litigants navigate the Court’s interpretive architecture for interpretive capture, invoking contradictory methods selectively at both the proceduralist and substantive levels while maintaining ideological consistency in their outcomes. What appears as methodological incoherence is the method itself; second, it reframes the relationship between the conservative civil society and the ECtHR as interpretive capture rather than backlash, revealing institutional and doctrinal vulnerabilities; and third, it demonstrates that what appears as methodological incoherence is, on closer examination, ideological coherence: the unit of consistency in conservative legal mobilisation is not method but outcome.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in firms is now close to universal, yet financial return remains concentrated in a small minority. This paper conducts a multivocal literature review, combining peer-reviewed research with 2025-2026 practitioner surveys and working papers, to examine why. It asks what current evidence shows about the relationship between AI adoption and value, which organizational capabilities distinguish firms that capture value, and how reliable the evidence base is. The evidence converges on four capabilities associated with value: workflow redesign, senior ownership, value tracking from the start, and people and change readiness. Governance appears as an enabler of scale rather than a brake on innovation: firms with stronger responsible AI foundations report more financial return, not less. The review also identifies a perception-value paradox, a systematic distance between the value executives perceive and the value measured in financial terms, visible between individual and enterprise levels, across sources and between expectations and outcomes. A critical appraisal shows that most practitioner evidence is self-reported and produced by firms with a commercial interest in transformation, which limits causal inference. The paper proposes five testable propositions linking organizational capabilities, governance maturity, scaling and value measurement, and outlines implications for boards, with attention to the Brazilian context, where stated confidence in AI is high and investment remains low.

detail.abstract: This working paper examines how trade, oil and monetary shocks were transmitted to the Congolese economy between 1909 and 1980, and how quickly the affected sectors regained their previous level of activity. The study combines a historical chronology covering the whole period with an analysis of annual data for 1960–1980. It brings together the reports of the issuing institutions, the national accounts and world prices for copper, oil and four agricultural commodities. The first oil shock raised the net oil import bill from 1.6% of GDP in 1972 to about 3.9% in 1974. In 1975, the real world price of copper fell by 46.0%, while the tonnage produced in Zaire declined by less than 1%. Recovery then depends on the indicator considered. Goods exports regained their 1974 value in current dollars as early as 1979. In 1980, however, their purchasing power over manufactured goods was still 19.9% below its 1974 level, and real GDP 21.2% below. Agriculture followed a different path. Its real value added regained its 1974 level in 1976, whereas palm oil exports remained persistently depressed. With twenty annual changes, the estimates remain too imprecise to attribute a distinct share of the GDP contraction to each shock. The Congolese experience thus reveals lasting gaps between the recovery of foreign-exchange earnings, import capacity and domestic output.

detail.abstract: Investment committees and corporate leaders devote considerable resources to quantifying business plans, challenging financial assumptions and evaluating individual executives. Yet a fundamental question often remains unanswered: how do we measure the collective responsible for executing those plans? A team may consist of highly qualified individuals without necessarily possessing the collective configuration best suited to the execution demands of a specific strategy. This paper examines that measurement gap and introduces a structured, ex-ante approach to Collective Execution Fit, using the PHCI (Paralipse Human Capital Intelligence) measurement system. The approach distinguishes three dimensions -Growth Execution, Productivity Execution and Operating Execution-derived from defined collective- level indicators. These measures are interpreted alongside quantified business objectives while remaining mathematically independent of financial targets. The paper presents the underlying measurement architecture, scoring conventions and an illustrative application. It also introduces a longitudinal approach for reassessing collective configurations as business plans and organizations evolve. Rather than predicting financial outcomes, the proposed methodology provides a reproducible framework for making collective execution characteristics visible, comparable and open to further investigation. Its central contribution is to establish the collective itself as a distinct unit of measurement in value creation, investment decision-making and business transformation, while identifying the empirical validation required to examine its practical significance.

detail.abstract: Using a comprehensive sample of U.S. M&A deals from 2000 through 2020, we examine whether the magnitude of policy uncertainty can explain the likelihood of deal cancellation. Consistent with our conjecture, we find that policy uncertainty is a significant predictor of the death of deals. Moreover, we find evidence of a negative association between policy uncertainty and the target firm stock price levels, implying that the market also incorporates the consequences of policy uncertainty into target valuation and bid likelihood outcomes. Altogether, our findings add to the understanding of the interplay between policy uncertainty and external investments through M&A.

detail.abstract:
This paper applies Henry Hansmann's transaction-cost theory of enterprise ownership to systemically important banks. Hansmann argues that ownership should be allocated to the stakeholder group that can minimize the sum of the costs of market contracting and the costs of ownership. For most firms, this points to investor ownership, as investors tend to share similar interests and can therefore make collective decisions at low cost.

The paper argues that systemic banks are an exception. Their costs of market contracting with creditors are exceptionally high, owing to information asymmetry and oligopolistic market features. Implicit and explicit government guarantees hide part of these costs by shifting them to deposit insurers and taxpayers. Because creditors provide most of a bank's funding, the costs are also much larger in absolute terms than the costs of contracting with shareholders. Once these costs are taken into account in full, Hansmann's framework supports transferring some ownership and control rights from shareholders to creditors. The rights should be attached to a standardized debt instrument, whose holders can act as a proxy for creditors more generally while keeping the costs of collective decision-making low. The paper also argues that Hansmann's explanation for the decline of depositor-owned savings banks is less convincing for modern systemic banks, and it considers the costs of shared governance between shareholders and creditors.

detail.abstract: The Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022 set off Europe's largest rearmament since the Cold War. For investors committed to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) objectives, the war has created a tension: can defense stocks be part of a sustainable portfolio, and will these investors help finance the build-up? Using confidential security-level holdings from the ECB's Securities Holdings Statistics for 2013-2026, covering over 34,000 listed firms held by different investor sectors from 24 European countries, we trace who rearmed their portfolios. We find that European investors raised their ownership shares in defense stocks after the invasion and in periods of increased geopolitical risk. This rearming of the portfolio is concentrated among investors with weak ESG orientation: investor groups whose prewar portfolios ranked in the top quartile of ESG scores did not increase their defense ownership. The gap persisted after the European Commission's 2025 Notice, which clarified that EU sustainable finance rules do not require investors to exclude defense companies. Institutional investors broadly increased their defense holdings after the EU Notice, especially in European firms, but those with high ESG scores did not. So far, regulatory clarification alone has not brought sustainable investors into Europe's defense build-up.

detail.abstract: Understanding how pricing strategies shape consumer choices is crucial in modern retail, particularly when engaging young consumers. This research paper investigates how four major pricing strategies-discounting, psychological pricing (odd-even), premium quality signaling, and product bundling-influence the purchasing decisions of urban teenagers in Mumbai. Utilizing a quantitative research design, empirical data was gathered through a structured survey from 63 respondents, predominantly aged 15 to 18, operating under limited monthly pocket money allowances. The data was evaluated using descriptive metrics, Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit tests, and One-Sample t-tests against a neutral baseline. The findings reveal that teenagers are highly responsive to volume-based incentives; Buy-One-Get-One Free (BOGO) promotions significantly outperform flat percentage cuts. Additionally, left-digit psychological pricing (₹99 vs. ₹100) creates a strong perception of affordability, and higher prices strongly signal superior quality. Product bundling also proved highly effective, with 71.43% preferring bulk bundle offers. Despite active price-comparison habits, teens demonstrate high tolerance for minor price hikes. These insights provide retail marketers with actionable strategies to tailor promotional tactics for Gen-Z shoppers in emerging urban markets.
